interviewBank.q: Hex or HSL — which do you choose and why?
interviewBank.answer: Hex is compact and familiar for fixed brand values. HSL is easier to reason about when deriving variants, because hue, saturation and lightness are separate numbers.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between background and background-color?
interviewBank.answer: background is a shorthand that resets every background property; background-color sets only the colour. Using the shorthand after a colour can wipe the earlier layer.

interviewBank.q: How do you keep text readable on a gradient?
interviewBank.answer: Check contrast against the darkest and lightest part of the gradient, add a solid overlay behind the text, and never assume the middle of a gradient is the worst case.

interviewBank.q: How does a three-digit hex colour expand?
interviewBank.answer: Each digit is doubled, so #f0a becomes #ff00aa; the shorthand is valid only when both digits of every pair are identical.

interviewBank.q: What does an eight-digit hex colour add?
interviewBank.answer: The final pair is alpha, so #2563ebcc is the blue #2563eb at roughly eighty percent opacity.

interviewBank.q: What is the space-separated rgb() syntax?
interviewBank.answer: It writes channels without commas and puts alpha after a slash, such as rgb(37 99 235 / 0.8), which is the modern form.

interviewBank.q: How is hsl() written?
interviewBank.answer: Hue in degrees, saturation and lightness as percentages, with optional alpha after a slash, such as hsl(221 83% 53% / 0.9).

interviewBank.q: What does the color() function allow?
interviewBank.answer: It selects an explicit colour space, such as display-p3, which can express colours outside the sRGB gamut on capable displays.

interviewBank.q: Why use oklch() instead of hsl()?
interviewBank.answer: OKLCH is perceptually uniform, so changing lightness or hue behaves more predictably and a palette keeps even contrast steps.

interviewBank.q: What does color-mix() do?
interviewBank.answer: It blends two colours in a chosen colour space, which is useful for deriving hover or tint variants from a single token.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between opacity and an alpha colour?
interviewBank.answer: opacity fades the whole element including its children and border, while an alpha colour fades only that one paint.

interviewBank.q: What does currentColor refer to?
interviewBank.answer: It resolves to the element's computed color, so a border or icon can follow the text colour without repeating the value.

interviewBank.q: Is transparent the same as a transparent black?
interviewBank.answer: transparent is a named colour equal to transparent black, but using it as a background can still change how blending and shadows behave.

interviewBank.q: Why are named colours risky for a design system?
interviewBank.answer: Names are limited and inconsistent across palettes, so a brand token expressed as a name is harder to adjust and version than a value.

interviewBank.q: What is a contrast ratio?
interviewBank.answer: A ratio between the relative luminance of two colours, from 1:1 to 21:1, used to judge whether text is readable against its background.

interviewBank.q: What contrast does WCAG AA require for normal text?
interviewBank.answer: At least 4.5:1 for normal-size text, measured between the text colour and the actual background behind it.

interviewBank.q: What contrast is required for large text?
interviewBank.answer: At least 3:1, because larger glyphs remain legible at a lower ratio than body-size text.

interviewBank.q: What does background-color set?
interviewBank.answer: The solid colour painted behind an element's content and padding, below any background image and inside the border box.

interviewBank.q: How do multiple background images stack?
interviewBank.answer: The first layer in the list paints on top, and later layers paint beneath it, so an overlay gradient is written before the photo.

interviewBank.q: What does background-repeat control?
interviewBank.answer: Whether and how an image tiles across the background; no-repeat shows one copy, while repeat-x or repeat-y tiles in one direction.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between background-size cover and contain?
interviewBank.answer: cover fills the box and may crop the image, while contain shows the whole image and may leave empty space.

interviewBank.q: What does background-position do?
interviewBank.answer: It places the image within the painting area, using keywords, lengths or percentages, often combined with cover to choose the crop focus.

interviewBank.q: What does background-attachment: fixed do?
interviewBank.answer: It fixes the background to the viewport so it does not move with the element's scroll, an effect that is often expensive on mobile.

interviewBank.q: Why is the background shorthand dangerous after setting a colour?
interviewBank.answer: It resets every background longhand it owns, so a later shorthand without a colour can wipe the colour you set earlier.

interviewBank.q: How do you set the direction of a linear gradient?
interviewBank.answer: Use an angle or a side keyword, such as linear-gradient(135deg, ...) or linear-gradient(to right, ...), before the colour stops.

interviewBank.q: How is a radial gradient positioned?
interviewBank.answer: Its centre and shape are set before the stops, such as radial-gradient(circle at 30% 30%, ...), which changes where the colour bloom begins.

interviewBank.q: What is a conic gradient useful for?
interviewBank.answer: It sweeps colour around a centre point, which suits pie charts, colour wheels and angular progress indicators.

interviewBank.q: What is a colour stop?
interviewBank.answer: A colour paired with an optional position along the gradient line, which tells the browser where that colour must be reached.

interviewBank.q: What is a hard stop in a gradient?
interviewBank.answer: Two stops at the same position create an abrupt edge instead of a blend, which can draw stripes or a sharp split background.

interviewBank.q: When do you use a repeating gradient?
interviewBank.answer: When a small pattern must tile across a larger area, such as stripes or a progress track, using repeating-linear-gradient with a short cycle.

interviewBank.q: Why does a gradient sometimes show banding?
interviewBank.answer: Too few colour steps across a large area reveal the 8-bit quantization, which can be reduced with subtle noise, dithering or a smoother colour space.

interviewBank.q: How do you place text over a photo reliably?
interviewBank.answer: Paint a semi-transparent gradient or solid overlay as the top background layer, then choose a text colour that contrasts with the darkest part of that overlay.

interviewBank.q: Why set a background colour when using a background image?
interviewBank.answer: If the image fails or loads slowly, the fallback colour keeps the text on a deliberate surface instead of the browser default.

interviewBank.q: What does background-blend-mode do?
interviewBank.answer: It blends an element's background layers with each other, such as multiplying a texture into a colour, without affecting the content above them.

interviewBank.q: How is filter different from backdrop-filter?
interviewBank.answer: filter affects the element's own rendering, while backdrop-filter blurs or adjusts whatever is painted behind the element.

interviewBank.q: How do you design colours for dark mode?
interviewBank.answer: Define semantic tokens, then override their values in a dark scope; pure inversion is avoided because saturated colours and shadows behave differently on dark surfaces.

interviewBank.q: What are CSS system colours?
interviewBank.answer: Keywords such as Canvas and CanvasText that follow the user's operating-system theme, which help a page fit forced-colours and high-contrast modes.

interviewBank.q: What is forced-colors mode?
interviewBank.answer: A user setting where the browser replaces author colours with a limited system palette, so designs must keep borders, focus and meaning visible without colour alone.

interviewBank.q: Why does print need different colour decisions?
interviewBank.answer: Printers handle ink and paper differently, backgrounds are often not printed, and light text on a dark background can become unreadable or waste ink.

interviewBank.q: What is colour management in CSS?
interviewBank.answer: The browser maps declared colours into the display's colour space, which is why a wide-gamut P3 colour can look different from the same sRGB value.

interviewBank.q: Why keep a palette of raw colour tokens?
interviewBank.answer: A small named palette gives one place to adjust values, while components reference semantic tokens built from it instead of inventing new hex codes.

interviewBank.q: What is a semantic colour token?
interviewBank.answer: A name that describes a role, such as surface or danger, rather than a hue, so the value can change with theme while the meaning stays stable.

interviewBank.q: Which tools help verify contrast?
interviewBank.answer: Browser DevTools' contrast readout, dedicated contrast checkers and automated accessibility audits, always measured against the real rendered background.

interviewBank.q: How do you make gradient text?
interviewBank.answer: Clip the background to the text and make the text transparent, but keep a solid fallback because the technique can fail in forced-colours or older engines.

interviewBank.q: Why can large background images hurt performance?
interviewBank.answer: They add download and decode cost, and a fixed or repainting background can force expensive work during scroll, especially on mobile GPUs.

interviewBank.q: Why is colour alone a poor way to convey meaning?
interviewBank.answer: Readers with colour-vision deficiency, monochrome screens or forced-colours mode lose the distinction, so pair colour with text, icons, weight or pattern.

defenseBank.q: A learner picks colours by eye only.
defenseBank.answer: I check contrast with a tool, because a colour that looks fine on one monitor fails for low-vision users and in bright light.

defenseBank.q: Why set a fallback background colour with an image?
defenseBank.answer: If the image fails or is slow, the text still sits on a deliberate surface instead of the browser default.

interviewBank.q: rem or em — when do you use each?
interviewBank.answer: rem for anything that should follow the root scale: type, spacing, radii. em when a component should scale relative to its own font size, such as padding on a button.

interviewBank.q: Why can 100vw cause a horizontal scrollbar?
interviewBank.answer: On desktop vw includes the vertical scrollbar width, while the content area does not. 100% follows the containing block and avoids the mismatch.

interviewBank.q: What does clamp actually do?
interviewBank.answer: clamp(min, preferred, max) returns the preferred value, but never below the minimum or above the maximum. It is the standard way to make type fluid without media queries.

interviewBank.q: What is a CSS pixel?
interviewBank.answer: A logical unit resolved against the display's reference pixel, not a guarantee of one physical device pixel, which is why high-density screens scale it.

interviewBank.q: What does rem measure?
interviewBank.answer: The root element's computed font size, so one rem follows the user's base size instead of a hard-coded pixel value.

interviewBank.q: What does em measure?
interviewBank.answer: The element's own computed font size, or its parent's when used on font-size, which makes it relative and sometimes compounding.

interviewBank.q: A percentage width resolves against what?
interviewBank.answer: The containing block's width, so the same fifty percent is a different number of pixels in a narrow and a wide parent.

interviewBank.q: When are vw and vh useful?
interviewBank.answer: For sizes that should follow the viewport, such as a full-height hero or fluid type, though vw includes the scrollbar on desktop.

interviewBank.q: What do dvh, svh and lvh solve?
interviewBank.answer: They separate the dynamic, small and large viewport heights on mobile, where browser chrome changes the visible area during scroll.

interviewBank.q: When do vmin and vmax help?
interviewBank.answer: When a square or shape must follow the shorter or longer viewport side, so it stays proportional in both portrait and landscape.

interviewBank.q: What does the ch unit represent?
interviewBank.answer: The width of the zero glyph in the current font, which makes it a useful approximation for limiting a line to a number of characters.

interviewBank.q: What does ex measure?
interviewBank.answer: The x-height of the current font, a font-relative unit that is rarely used except for small optical adjustments.

interviewBank.q: What does fr mean in a grid track?
interviewBank.answer: A fraction of the free space left after fixed tracks and gaps, so 1fr and 2fr split that space in a one-to-two ratio.

interviewBank.q: Which CSS units are absolute?
interviewBank.answer: px, cm, mm, in, pt and pc are absolute in CSS terms, though px is still resolved against the reference pixel rather than a device dot.

interviewBank.q: When are physical units such as cm or pt still appropriate?
interviewBank.answer: For print stylesheets and documents that must match paper dimensions, not for screen layout where zoom and density vary.

interviewBank.q: What is the default root font size?
interviewBank.answer: Sixteen CSS pixels in most browsers, but it is a user preference, so rem-based layouts must not assume that number is fixed.

interviewBank.q: How does browser zoom interact with px and rem?
interviewBank.answer: Zoom scales the whole layout, but a user's font-size preference changes the root size, which rem respects and px ignores for text.

interviewBank.q: Why does nested em sizing compound?
interviewBank.answer: Each level multiplies its parent's computed size, so two nested 1.2em elements produce 1.44 times the outer size instead of 1.2.

interviewBank.q: Why is line-height better left unitless?
interviewBank.answer: A unitless value multiplies the element's own font size, so nested text keeps the intended ratio instead of inheriting a fixed length.

interviewBank.q: What does calc() require around plus and minus?
interviewBank.answer: Whitespace on both sides of the operator, because without it the parser can read the sign as part of a number or identifier.

interviewBank.q: What does min() choose?
interviewBank.answer: The smallest of its arguments, allowing a width to shrink below a preferred value but never exceed a hard limit.

interviewBank.q: What does max() choose?
interviewBank.answer: The largest of its arguments, which is useful for a minimum size that still grows with available space.

interviewBank.q: What are the three parts of clamp()?
interviewBank.answer: A minimum, a preferred value and a maximum; the browser returns the preferred value bounded by the other two.

interviewBank.q: What does minmax() do in a grid track?
interviewBank.answer: It sets a track's minimum and maximum size, so a column can shrink no further than the first value and grow no larger than the second.

interviewBank.q: How does fit-content behave?
interviewBank.answer: It sizes to the content up to a limit, then stops growing, which is useful for chips and sidebars that should not stretch.

interviewBank.q: What does auto mean for width and height?
interviewBank.answer: It lets the browser resolve the size from the layout context, such as filling a block or sizing to content, rather than a fixed number.

interviewBank.q: Why is zero allowed without a unit?
interviewBank.answer: Zero is the same length in every unit, so the specification permits the bare number while other nonzero lengths require a unit.

interviewBank.q: What does percentage padding resolve against?
interviewBank.answer: The containing block's inline size, even for vertical padding, which is why percentage padding can create surprising aspect ratios.

interviewBank.q: Why does percentage height often fail?
interviewBank.answer: It needs a definite containing block height; if the parent's height is auto, the percentage has nothing to resolve against and is treated as auto.

interviewBank.q: What does aspect-ratio do?
interviewBank.answer: It sets a preferred width-to-height ratio, letting one dimension follow the other while the box remains responsive.

interviewBank.q: What are container query units?
interviewBank.answer: Units such as cqw and cqh that resolve against the nearest query container instead of the viewport, so a component can scale with its own space.

interviewBank.q: Can media queries use rem?
interviewBank.answer: Yes, and doing so ties breakpoints to the user's root font size, so a reader who enlarges text gets the layout intended for a wider screen.

interviewBank.q: Why keep borders in px?
interviewBank.answer: A one-pixel border usually expresses a hairline regardless of text size, while spacing and type should follow the user's scale.

interviewBank.q: What are resolution units used for?
interviewBank.answer: dpi, dpcm and dppx describe pixel density, mainly in media queries for choosing sharper images on high-density displays.

interviewBank.q: What are angle units used for?
interviewBank.answer: deg, grad, rad and turn describe rotation and gradient direction, with turn being a convenient full circle.

interviewBank.q: What are time units used for?
interviewBank.answer: s and ms set transition and animation durations and delays; they are the only units accepted for those properties.

interviewBank.q: Why prefer fr over percentages in a grid?
interviewBank.answer: fr distributes the space left after gaps and fixed tracks, so tracks do not overflow when gaps are added.

interviewBank.q: Why are viewport units unreliable for mobile height?
interviewBank.answer: Mobile browser chrome changes the visible height during scroll, so vh can be taller than the actual visible area; dvh or svh reflect that behaviour.

interviewBank.q: How do you create fluid type?
interviewBank.answer: Use clamp() with a viewport-relative preferred value, bounded by a readable minimum and maximum, instead of fixing a size per breakpoint.

interviewBank.q: How do you create fluid spacing?
interviewBank.answer: Use clamp() or calc() on a spacing token, so gaps grow with the viewport within limits rather than jumping at breakpoints.

interviewBank.q: How do you convert between px and rem?
interviewBank.answer: Divide the pixel value by the root font size, usually sixteen, so 24px becomes 1.5rem; the conversion is a design aid, not a runtime rule.

interviewBank.q: Why can a px-based design fail accessibility?
interviewBank.answer: The text ignores the reader's font-size preference, so a user who enlarges text still sees the original size and may be unable to read it.

interviewBank.q: Why use rem for spacing as well as text?
interviewBank.answer: Spacing tied to the root scale keeps the rhythm proportional when the reader changes text size, instead of leaving cramped gaps around larger type.

interviewBank.q: Why is ch useful for a reading measure?
interviewBank.answer: A width in ch approximates characters per line, so a 65ch limit keeps a comfortable measure even when the font size changes.

interviewBank.q: How do you debug a unit mismatch?
interviewBank.answer: Inspect the Computed panel for the resolved pixel value, then trace which parent or font size the relative unit resolved against.

interviewBank.q: Which unit should a beginner default to?
interviewBank.answer: rem for type and spacing, percentages or fr for layout, and px for hairlines, then reach for viewport and container units only when the layout needs them.

defenseBank.q: A design uses px for every font size.
defenseBank.answer: px ignores the user’s font-size preference, which breaks zoom and accessibility. rem follows the root size and respects that setting.
steps: Change the browser default font size.
Switch to rem and show it scale.

defenseBank.q: Why is a unitless line-height safer?
defenseBank.answer: A unitless value multiplies the element’s own font size, so nested text keeps the intended ratio. A px line-height stays fixed and can overlap when the font grows.
steps: Show a large heading with 20px line-height.

mcqBank.q: What does 1rem equal by default?
mcqBank.why: The default root font size is 16px.

mcqBank.q: Which unit shares free space in a Grid track?
mcqBank.why: fr distributes the free space of the grid container.

interview.answer: clamp(min, preferred, max) returns the preferred value, but never below the minimum or above the maximum. It is the standard way to make type fluid without media queries.

interview.q: What is a CSS pixel?
interview.answer: A logical unit resolved against the display's reference pixel, not a guarantee of one physical device pixel, which is why high-density screens scale it.

interview.q: What does rem measure?
interview.answer: The root element's computed font size, so one rem follows the user's base size instead of a hard-coded pixel value.

interview.q: What does em measure?
interview.answer: The element's own computed font size, or its parent's when used on font-size, which makes it relative and sometimes compounding.

interview.q: A percentage width resolves against what?
interview.answer: The containing block's width, so the same fifty percent is a different number of pixels in a narrow and a wide parent.

interview.q: When are vw and vh useful?
interview.answer: For sizes that should follow the viewport, such as a full-height hero or fluid type, though vw includes the scrollbar on desktop.

interview.q: What do dvh, svh and lvh solve?
interview.answer: They separate the dynamic, small and large viewport heights on mobile, where browser chrome changes the visible area during scroll.

interview.q: When do vmin and vmax help?
interview.answer: When a square or shape must follow the shorter or longer viewport side, so it stays proportional in both portrait and landscape.

interview.q: What does the ch unit represent?
interview.answer: The width of the zero glyph in the current font, which makes it a useful approximation for limiting a line to a number of characters.

interview.q: What does ex measure?
interview.answer: The x-height of the current font, a font-relative unit that is rarely used except for small optical adjustments.

interview.q: What does fr mean in a grid track?
interview.answer: A fraction of the free space left after fixed tracks and gaps, so 1fr and 2fr split that space in a one-to-two ratio.

interview.q: Which CSS units are absolute?
interview.answer: px, cm, mm, in, pt and pc are absolute in CSS terms, though px is still resolved against the reference pixel rather than a device dot.

interview.q: When are physical units such as cm or pt still appropriate?
interview.answer: For print stylesheets and documents that must match paper dimensions, not for screen layout where zoom and density vary.

interview.q: What is the default root font size?
interview.answer: Sixteen CSS pixels in most browsers, but it is a user preference, so rem-based layouts must not assume that number is fixed.

interview.q: How does browser zoom interact with px and rem?
interview.answer: Zoom scales the whole layout, but a user's font-size preference changes the root size, which rem respects and px ignores for text.

interview.q: Why does nested em sizing compound?
interview.answer: Each level multiplies its parent's computed size, so two nested 1.2em elements produce 1.44 times the outer size instead of 1.2.

interview.q: Why is line-height better left unitless?
interview.answer: A unitless value multiplies the element's own font size, so nested text keeps the intended ratio instead of inheriting a fixed length.

interview.q: What does calc() require around plus and minus?
interview.answer: Whitespace on both sides of the operator, because without it the parser can read the sign as part of a number or identifier.

interview.q: What does min() choose?
interview.answer: The smallest of its arguments, allowing a width to shrink below a preferred value but never exceed a hard limit.

interview.q: What does max() choose?
interview.answer: The largest of its arguments, which is useful for a minimum size that still grows with available space.

interview.q: What are the three parts of clamp()?
interview.answer: A minimum, a preferred value and a maximum; the browser returns the preferred value bounded by the other two.

interview.q: What does minmax() do in a grid track?
interview.answer: It sets a track's minimum and maximum size, so a column can shrink no further than the first value and grow no larger than the second.

interview.q: How does fit-content behave?
interview.answer: It sizes to the content up to a limit, then stops growing, which is useful for chips and sidebars that should not stretch.

interview.q: What does auto mean for width and height?
interview.answer: It lets the browser resolve the size from the layout context, such as filling a block or sizing to content, rather than a fixed number.

interview.q: Why is zero allowed without a unit?
interview.answer: Zero is the same length in every unit, so the specification permits the bare number while other nonzero lengths require a unit.

interview.q: What does percentage padding resolve against?
interview.answer: The containing block's inline size, even for vertical padding, which is why percentage padding can create surprising aspect ratios.

interview.q: Why does percentage height often fail?
interview.answer: It needs a definite containing block height; if the parent's height is auto, the percentage has nothing to resolve against and is treated as auto.

interview.q: What does aspect-ratio do?
interview.answer: It sets a preferred width-to-height ratio, letting one dimension follow the other while the box remains responsive.

interview.q: What are container query units?
interview.answer: Units such as cqw and cqh that resolve against the nearest query container instead of the viewport, so a component can scale with its own space.

interview.q: Can media queries use rem?
interview.answer: Yes, and doing so ties breakpoints to the user's root font size, so a reader who enlarges text gets the layout intended for a wider screen.

interview.q: Why keep borders in px?
interview.answer: A one-pixel border usually expresses a hairline regardless of text size, while spacing and type should follow the user's scale.

interview.q: What are resolution units used for?
interview.answer: dpi, dpcm and dppx describe pixel density, mainly in media queries for choosing sharper images on high-density displays.

interview.q: What are angle units used for?
interview.answer: deg, grad, rad and turn describe rotation and gradient direction, with turn being a convenient full circle.

interview.q: What are time units used for?
interview.answer: s and ms set transition and animation durations and delays; they are the only units accepted for those properties.

interview.q: Why prefer fr over percentages in a grid?
interview.answer: fr distributes the space left after gaps and fixed tracks, so tracks do not overflow when gaps are added.

interview.q: Why are viewport units unreliable for mobile height?
interview.answer: Mobile browser chrome changes the visible height during scroll, so vh can be taller than the actual visible area; dvh or svh reflect that behaviour.

interview.q: How do you create fluid type?
interview.answer: Use clamp() with a viewport-relative preferred value, bounded by a readable minimum and maximum, instead of fixing a size per breakpoint.

interview.q: How do you create fluid spacing?
interview.answer: Use clamp() or calc() on a spacing token, so gaps grow with the viewport within limits rather than jumping at breakpoints.

interview.q: How do you convert between px and rem?
interview.answer: Divide the pixel value by the root font size, usually sixteen, so 24px becomes 1.5rem; the conversion is a design aid, not a runtime rule.

interview.q: Why can a px-based design fail accessibility?
interview.answer: The text ignores the reader's font-size preference, so a user who enlarges text still sees the original size and may be unable to read it.

interview.q: Why use rem for spacing as well as text?
interview.answer: Spacing tied to the root scale keeps the rhythm proportional when the reader changes text size, instead of leaving cramped gaps around larger type.

interview.q: Why is ch useful for a reading measure?
interview.answer: A width in ch approximates characters per line, so a 65ch limit keeps a comfortable measure even when the font size changes.

interview.q: How do you debug a unit mismatch?
interview.answer: Inspect the Computed panel for the resolved pixel value, then trace which parent or font size the relative unit resolved against.

interview.q: Which unit should a beginner default to?
interview.answer: rem for type and spacing, percentages or fr for layout, and px for hairlines, then reach for viewport and container units only when the layout needs them.

interviewBank.q: Why does font-family take a list?
interviewBank.answer: The browser uses the first family it can actually render. The list ends with a generic family so the page never falls back to an unrelated default.

interviewBank.q: Why is line-height usually unitless?
interviewBank.answer: A unitless number multiplies the element’s own font size, so it scales with nested text instead of staying a fixed length.

interviewBank.q: What is FOUT and how do you reduce it?
interviewBank.answer: Flash of unstyled text: fallback text is shown before the web font loads, then swaps. Preloading the font, using font-display and choosing a close fallback reduce the visible shift.

interviewBank.q: Why does font-family take an ordered stack?
interviewBank.answer: The browser uses the first family it can render, so the order decides which available font wins before the generic fallback is reached.

interviewBank.q: Why must every stack end in a generic family?
interviewBank.answer: A generic family is guaranteed to exist, so the page still gets a sensible serif, sans-serif or monospace instead of the browser's arbitrary default.

interviewBank.q: What is a web font?
interviewBank.answer: A font file delivered by the page and declared with @font-face, which gives a consistent typeface instead of relying on installed fonts.

interviewBank.q: What does @font-face declare?
interviewBank.answer: A font family name, one or more sources with formats, and descriptors such as weight, style and display behaviour.

interviewBank.q: What does font-display control?
interviewBank.answer: How a web font behaves while it loads: swap shows fallback text immediately, block hides text briefly, and optional avoids late swaps.

interviewBank.q: Why preload a font file?
interviewBank.answer: Preloading starts the request before the CSS that references it is parsed, which reduces the delay before the first text paint.

interviewBank.q: What is a flash of invisible text?
interviewBank.answer: A period where the browser hides text while waiting for a web font, usually caused by a block period in font-display.

interviewBank.q: What do numeric font-weight values mean?
interviewBank.answer: They range from 100 to 900 in increasing boldness, and a variable font can interpolate between them instead of jumping to named weights.

interviewBank.q: What is a variable font?
interviewBank.answer: A single font file with axes for weight, width or slant, so the page can request intermediate values without downloading several files.

interviewBank.q: What does font-style control?
interviewBank.answer: Whether the face is normal, italic or oblique, and the browser may synthesise a slant if the family lacks a real italic.

interviewBank.q: Why use a type scale instead of arbitrary sizes?
interviewBank.answer: A small set of related sizes creates hierarchy and rhythm, while one-off font sizes make the page look uneven and hard to maintain.

interviewBank.q: Why express type sizes in rem?
interviewBank.answer: rem follows the reader's root preference, so the whole scale grows together when the default font size is increased.

interviewBank.q: What does line-height: normal mean?
interviewBank.answer: The font's own recommended line spacing, which varies by typeface and is rarely the value a designer wants for body text.

interviewBank.q: What is a readable measure?
interviewBank.answer: Roughly 45 to 75 characters per line, often limited with ch, because lines that are too long or too short slow reading.

interviewBank.q: What does letter-spacing change?
interviewBank.answer: The space between characters; small positive values can help uppercase labels, while large values hurt word recognition.

interviewBank.q: What does word-spacing change?
interviewBank.answer: The space between words, which is rarely adjusted except for justified text or a specific display treatment.

interviewBank.q: What does text-align affect?
interviewBank.answer: The alignment of inline content inside its block, such as left, right, center or justify, not the position of the block itself.

interviewBank.q: How do you remove an underline from a link accessibly?
interviewBank.answer: Remove it only when another clear affordance remains, and always keep a visible focus and hover state so the link is still recognisable.

interviewBank.q: What does text-transform do?
interviewBank.answer: It changes the rendered case without changing the underlying text, so uppercase labels remain readable to screen readers and copy-paste.

interviewBank.q: How does text-shadow differ from box-shadow?
interviewBank.answer: text-shadow follows the glyph shapes and takes no spread or inset value, while box-shadow follows the element's box.

interviewBank.q: What does text-overflow require to work?
interviewBank.answer: A single-line box with overflow hidden and white-space nowrap, otherwise the text wraps and there is no overflow to ellipsise.

interviewBank.q: What does white-space control?
interviewBank.answer: Whether whitespace collapses, wraps or is preserved, which decides if text stays on one line or breaks at spaces.

interviewBank.q: What does overflow-wrap: anywhere do?
interviewBank.answer: It allows a long unbreakable string to break at any point when needed, preventing it from forcing the container wider.

interviewBank.q: How is word-break different from overflow-wrap?
interviewBank.answer: word-break changes the language's normal breaking rules, while overflow-wrap only intervenes when a word would otherwise overflow.

interviewBank.q: What does hyphens: auto do?
interviewBank.answer: It lets the browser insert language-aware hyphenation at line ends, which can improve justification but needs the correct lang attribute.

interviewBank.q: What does text-wrap: balance do?
interviewBank.answer: It distributes lines evenly in a short block such as a heading, avoiding a single orphan word on the last line.

interviewBank.q: What does font-variant control?
interviewBank.answer: It selects alternate glyph sets such as small caps or old-style numerals, a higher-level switch than raw font features.

interviewBank.q: How do you enable tabular numbers?
interviewBank.answer: Use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so digits share a width, which keeps columns of figures aligned.

interviewBank.q: How do you style a drop cap?
interviewBank.answer: Use ::first-letter with a larger size and float, then check the line box so the cap does not collide with the first line.

interviewBank.q: What is vertical rhythm?
interviewBank.answer: A consistent baseline spacing derived from line-height, so headings, paragraphs and margins land on the same grid instead of drifting.

interviewBank.q: How do you make type responsive without breakpoints?
interviewBank.answer: Use clamp() with a viewport-relative middle value and a readable minimum and maximum, then test the extremes.

interviewBank.q: Why cap fluid type with clamp()?
interviewBank.answer: Without a maximum, headings become absurdly large on wide screens; without a minimum, body text becomes unreadable on small ones.

interviewBank.q: What text spacing does WCAG expect?
interviewBank.answer: Readers must be able to increase line height, paragraph spacing, letter spacing and word spacing without losing content or functionality.

interviewBank.q: Why is text contrast more than a colour choice?
interviewBank.answer: The final ratio depends on the actual background, overlays and states, so a colour that passes on white can fail on an image or a tinted card.

interviewBank.q: How do web fonts affect performance?
interviewBank.answer: They add requests and bytes, can delay text, and may cause layout shift when the fallback and web font have different metrics.

interviewBank.q: Why use system fonts on some projects?
interviewBank.answer: They load instantly, match the platform and avoid layout shift, which is often the better trade-off for utility interfaces.

interviewBank.q: Why prefer SVG icons over an icon font?
interviewBank.answer: SVG icons are individually accessible, styleable and crisp at any size, while icon fonts depend on private-use glyphs and can fail silently.

interviewBank.q: What are fallback font metrics?
interviewBank.answer: The measurements used to match a fallback closely to the web font, reducing the size and position shift when the real font swaps in.

interviewBank.q: When should a font be self-hosted?
interviewBank.answer: When the project needs control over privacy, caching and licensing, or the third-party font service is a performance or reliability risk.

interviewBank.q: What does font-smoothing change?
interviewBank.answer: It alters glyph antialiasing on some platforms, which can make text look thinner or heavier but is not a reliable cross-browser design control.

interviewBank.q: How do you debug a typography problem?
interviewBank.answer: Inspect the computed font family, size and line height, then check whether a fallback rendered, a rule was overridden, or the measure is wrong.

interviewBank.q: What are OpenType features in CSS?
interviewBank.answer: Optional glyph behaviours such as ligatures, fractions or stylistic sets, enabled with font-feature-settings or higher-level font-variant properties.

interviewBank.q: Why limit a paragraph with ch rather than px?
interviewBank.answer: ch scales with the font, so the measure stays proportional when the reader changes text size instead of becoming too wide or too narrow.

defenseBank.q: A learner sets body text to 12px to fit more.
defenseBank.answer: Small text costs readability and fails accessibility expectations. A 16px base with a wider measure and tighter spacing fits content without shrinking it.

defenseBank.q: Why cap the line length?
defenseBank.answer: Long lines make the eye lose its place on the return sweep; very short lines break rhythm. A 60–75 character measure is the readable range.

mcqBank.q: Which is a generic font family?
mcqBank.why: Generic families are the guaranteed fallbacks.

mcqBank.q: Which property adds space between letters?
mcqBank.why: letter-spacing adjusts space between characters.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between content-box and border-box?
interviewBank.answer: content-box adds padding and border outside the declared width. border-box includes them inside it, so width means the visible box. Most projects set border-box globally.

interviewBank.q: Why do vertical margins collapse?
interviewBank.answer: Adjacent block margins in normal flow combine into the larger of the two instead of adding, and a parent and first child can collapse too. Padding, borders, flex or grid contexts stop it.

interviewBank.q: What four layers does the CSS box model stack around an element's content?
interviewBank.answer: Content, padding, border and margin, from inside out; the background paints through content and padding but stops at the border.

interviewBank.q: Why does a box with padding and border look wider than its declared width by default?
interviewBank.answer: The default content-box sizing adds padding and border on top of the declared width, so the rendered box is wider than the number you wrote.

interviewBank.q: What does box-sizing: border-box change?
interviewBank.answer: It makes width and height include padding and border, so the declared size is the size the box actually occupies.

interviewBank.q: Which box-sizing value should a global reset usually choose?
interviewBank.answer: border-box, because it makes percentage and pixel widths predictable when padding and borders are added.

interviewBank.q: How is the margin of a block element different from its padding?
interviewBank.answer: Padding is inside the border and carries the background; margin is outside the border and is always transparent.

interviewBank.q: What is margin collapsing?
interviewBank.answer: Adjacent vertical margins of block elements merge into a single margin whose size is the larger of the two.

interviewBank.q: When do margins not collapse?
interviewBank.answer: They do not collapse when a parent has padding or a border, when elements are floated, positioned, flex or grid items, or when overflow creates a block formatting context.

interviewBank.q: What is a block formatting context?
interviewBank.answer: A region of layout in which block boxes are laid out independently, so floats and margins cannot leak across its boundary.

interviewBank.q: How do you create a block formatting context?
interviewBank.answer: Use overflow other than visible, display flow-root, or a flex or grid container; flow-root is the modern, side-effect-free choice.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between width and max-width?
interviewBank.answer: width sets a fixed size, while max-width caps the size but still lets the box shrink when the container is smaller.

interviewBank.q: Why use max-width: 100% on images?
interviewBank.answer: It keeps an image from overflowing its container while still allowing it to shrink to fit narrow viewports.

interviewBank.q: What does min-width do to a flex item?
interviewBank.answer: It sets a floor below which the item cannot shrink, which often causes overflow if the container is too small.

interviewBank.q: What is the initial value of box-sizing?
interviewBank.answer: content-box, which is why padding and border are added outside the declared width unless you override it.

interviewBank.q: How does padding affect an inline element?
interviewBank.answer: Vertical padding on an inline element paints but does not push other lines apart; horizontal padding does affect spacing.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between outline and border for layout?
interviewBank.answer: A border participates in box sizing and layout; an outline is drawn outside the border and never affects layout or box size.

interviewBank.q: Why might overflow: hidden clip content unexpectedly?
interviewBank.answer: It clips anything that extends beyond the padding box, including absolutely positioned descendants and box shadows.

interviewBank.q: What does overflow: auto do?
interviewBank.answer: It shows scrollbars only when content overflows, instead of always or never.

interviewBank.q: What is scroll chaining?
interviewBank.answer: When a nested scroll container reaches its limit, the scroll event propagates to the parent, which then scrolls.

interviewBank.q: How do you prevent scroll chaining?
interviewBank.answer: Apply overscroll-behavior: contain to the inner scroll container so it traps the scroll gesture.

interviewBank.q: How does box-sizing affect margin calculations?
interviewBank.answer: It does not; margins are always added outside the box regardless of box-sizing.

interviewBank.q: How is the containing block for a fixed element determined?
interviewBank.answer: Usually the viewport, unless an ancestor has a transform, filter or perspective, which then becomes the containing block.

interviewBank.q: What does z-index actually compare?
interviewBank.answer: It compares stacking levels only among elements that share the same stacking context and are positioned or otherwise eligible.

interviewBank.q: Why might a high z-index not bring an element to the front?
interviewBank.answer: Because z-index is scoped to the stacking context of its ancestor; a parent with a lower stacking context traps it.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between content-box and border-box for padding?
interviewBank.answer: content-box adds padding outside the declared width; border-box includes it.

interviewBank.q: How does margin: auto center a block horizontally?
interviewBank.answer: It splits the leftover horizontal space equally between the left and right margins of a block with a defined width.

interviewBank.q: Why does margin: auto not center vertically in normal flow?
interviewBank.answer: Vertical auto margins resolve to zero in normal flow; vertical centering needs flexbox, grid or absolute positioning.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between em and rem in spacing?
interviewBank.answer: em is relative to the element's own font size, so nested padding compounds; rem is relative to the root, so it stays consistent.

interviewBank.q: Why might em-based padding grow unexpectedly?
interviewBank.answer: Because an em on padding resolves against the element's computed font size, which can be larger than the parent's.

interviewBank.q: Why does vertical percentage padding depend on width?
interviewBank.answer: The specification resolves all percentage padding against the containing block's width, including top and bottom.

interviewBank.q: Why is percentage-based vertical padding useful for aspect ratios?
interviewBank.answer: Because padding-top or padding-bottom as a percentage of width creates a box whose height tracks its width.

interviewBank.q: What is the aspect-ratio property?
interviewBank.answer: It sets a preferred width-to-height ratio so the browser can reserve space before the content loads.

interviewBank.q: How do you make a square with CSS?
interviewBank.answer: Set aspect-ratio: 1 / 1, or use padding-bottom: 100% on a relatively positioned wrapper.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between display: none and visibility: hidden?
interviewBank.answer: display: none removes the element from layout; visibility: hidden keeps its space but hides its rendering.

interviewBank.q: Why might a hidden element still affect layout?
interviewBank.answer: visibility: hidden keeps the box in the flow, so siblings do not move; only display: none frees the space.

interviewBank.q: What is the initial containing block?
interviewBank.answer: The rectangle based on the viewport for continuous media, used when no positioned ancestor exists.

interviewBank.q: How does position: sticky decide when to stick?
interviewBank.answer: It behaves like relative until the scroll position crosses the specified inset, then sticks within its containing block.

interviewBank.q: What happens to margins when a parent has overflow: hidden?
interviewBank.answer: The parent establishes a block formatting context, so child margins no longer collapse with the parent's.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between min-content and max-content?
interviewBank.answer: min-content is the smallest size the content can take without overflow; max-content is the size if no soft wrapping occurs.

interviewBank.q: When would you use fit-content?
interviewBank.answer: When you want a box to size to its content but never exceed a given maximum, like fit-content(300px).

interviewBank.q: What does the box-decoration-break property control?
interviewBank.answer: It decides whether borders, padding and backgrounds are applied per fragment or across the whole element when it breaks across lines or pages.

interviewBank.q: Why might a box shadow be clipped by overflow: hidden?
interviewBank.answer: The shadow paints outside the padding box, so an ancestor with overflow: hidden clips it unless you add padding or change overflow.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between margin and gap?
interviewBank.answer: Margin pushes individual boxes apart and can collapse; gap adds space only between items in flex or grid containers and never collapses.

interviewBank.q: How does gap behave in a single-column flex layout?
interviewBank.answer: It adds vertical space between flex items without affecting the outer edges of the container.

interviewBank.q: What is the effect of box-sizing on replaced elements like images?
interviewBank.answer: It still applies, but the intrinsic size and aspect ratio of the replaced content may override the declared dimensions.

interviewBank.q: Why should you avoid negative margins for layout in modern CSS?
interviewBank.answer: They can pull elements out of flow and break stacking and spacing; flexbox and grid gap are clearer and safer.

defenseBank.q: A learner sets width 100% and gets a scrollbar.
defenseBank.answer: The padding and border are being added outside the width. border-box makes the declared width include them, which is why it is the usual global reset.

defenseBank.q: Why not use margins for inner spacing?
defenseBank.answer: Margin is outside the border and can collapse with neighbours; padding is inside and belongs to the element’s own surface.

interview.q: What is the difference between content-box and border-box?
interview.answer: content-box adds padding and border outside the declared width. border-box includes them inside it, so width means the visible box. Most projects set border-box globally.

interview.q: Why do vertical margins collapse?
interview.answer: Adjacent block margins in normal flow combine into the larger of the two instead of adding, and a parent and first child can collapse too. Padding, borders, flex or grid contexts stop it.

interview.q: What four layers does the CSS box model stack around an element's content?
interview.answer: Content, padding, border and margin, from inside out; the background paints through content and padding but stops at the border.

interview.q: Why does a box with padding and border look wider than its declared width by default?
interview.answer: The default content-box sizing adds padding and border on top of the declared width, so the rendered box is wider than the number you wrote.

interview.q: What does box-sizing: border-box change?
interview.answer: It makes width and height include padding and border, so the declared size is the size the box actually occupies.

interview.q: Which box-sizing value should a global reset usually choose?
interview.answer: border-box, because it makes percentage and pixel widths predictable when padding and borders are added.

interview.q: How is the margin of a block element different from its padding?
interview.answer: Padding is inside the border and carries the background; margin is outside the border and is always transparent.

interview.q: What is margin collapsing?
interview.answer: Adjacent vertical margins of block elements merge into a single margin whose size is the larger of the two.

interview.q: When do margins not collapse?
interview.answer: They do not collapse when a parent has padding or a border, when elements are floated, positioned, flex or grid items, or when overflow creates a block formatting context.

interview.q: What is a block formatting context?
interview.answer: A region of layout in which block boxes are laid out independently, so floats and margins cannot leak across its boundary.

interview.q: How do you create a block formatting context?
interview.answer: Use overflow other than visible, display flow-root, or a flex or grid container; flow-root is the modern, side-effect-free choice.

interview.q: What is the difference between width and max-width?
interview.answer: width sets a fixed size, while max-width caps the size but still lets the box shrink when the container is smaller.

interview.q: Why use max-width: 100% on images?
interview.answer: It keeps an image from overflowing its container while still allowing it to shrink to fit narrow viewports.

interview.q: What does min-width do to a flex item?
interview.answer: It sets a floor below which the item cannot shrink, which often causes overflow if the container is too small.

interview.q: What is the initial value of box-sizing?
interview.answer: content-box, which is why padding and border are added outside the declared width unless you override it.

interview.q: How does padding affect an inline element?
interview.answer: Vertical padding on an inline element paints but does not push other lines apart; horizontal padding does affect spacing.

interview.q: What is the difference between outline and border for layout?
interview.answer: A border participates in box sizing and layout; an outline is drawn outside the border and never affects layout or box size.

interview.q: Why might overflow: hidden clip content unexpectedly?
interview.answer: It clips anything that extends beyond the padding box, including absolutely positioned descendants and box shadows.

interview.q: What does overflow: auto do?
interview.answer: It shows scrollbars only when content overflows, instead of always or never.

interview.q: What is scroll chaining?
interview.answer: When a nested scroll container reaches its limit, the scroll event propagates to the parent, which then scrolls.

interview.q: How do you prevent scroll chaining?
interview.answer: Apply overscroll-behavior: contain to the inner scroll container so it traps the scroll gesture.

interview.q: How does box-sizing affect margin calculations?
interview.answer: It does not; margins are always added outside the box regardless of box-sizing.

interview.q: How is the containing block for a fixed element determined?
interview.answer: Usually the viewport, unless an ancestor has a transform, filter or perspective, which then becomes the containing block.

interview.q: What does z-index actually compare?
interview.answer: It compares stacking levels only among elements that share the same stacking context and are positioned or otherwise eligible.

interview.q: Why might a high z-index not bring an element to the front?
interview.answer: Because z-index is scoped to the stacking context of its ancestor; a parent with a lower stacking context traps it.

interview.q: What is the difference between content-box and border-box for padding?
interview.answer: content-box adds padding outside the declared width; border-box includes it.

interview.q: How does margin: auto center a block horizontally?
interview.answer: It splits the leftover horizontal space equally between the left and right margins of a block with a defined width.

interview.q: Why does margin: auto not center vertically in normal flow?
interview.answer: Vertical auto margins resolve to zero in normal flow; vertical centering needs flexbox, grid or absolute positioning.

interview.q: What is the difference between em and rem in spacing?
interview.answer: em is relative to the element's own font size, so nested padding compounds; rem is relative to the root, so it stays consistent.

interview.q: Why might em-based padding grow unexpectedly?
interview.answer: Because an em on padding resolves against the element's computed font size, which can be larger than the parent's.

interview.q: Why does vertical percentage padding depend on width?
interview.answer: The specification resolves all percentage padding against the containing block's width, including top and bottom.

interview.q: Why is percentage-based vertical padding useful for aspect ratios?
interview.answer: Because padding-top or padding-bottom as a percentage of width creates a box whose height tracks its width.

interview.q: What is the aspect-ratio property?
interview.answer: It sets a preferred width-to-height ratio so the browser can reserve space before the content loads.

interview.q: How do you make a square with CSS?
interview.answer: Set aspect-ratio: 1 / 1, or use padding-bottom: 100% on a relatively positioned wrapper.

interview.q: What is the difference between display: none and visibility: hidden?
interview.answer: display: none removes the element from layout; visibility: hidden keeps its space but hides its rendering.

interview.q: Why might a hidden element still affect layout?
interview.answer: visibility: hidden keeps the box in the flow, so siblings do not move; only display: none frees the space.

interview.q: What is the initial containing block?
interview.answer: The rectangle based on the viewport for continuous media, used when no positioned ancestor exists.

interview.q: How does position: sticky decide when to stick?
interview.answer: It behaves like relative until the scroll position crosses the specified inset, then sticks within its containing block.

interview.q: What happens to margins when a parent has overflow: hidden?
interview.answer: The parent establishes a block formatting context, so child margins no longer collapse with the parent's.

interview.q: What is the difference between min-content and max-content?
interview.answer: min-content is the smallest size the content can take without overflow; max-content is the size if no soft wrapping occurs.

interview.q: When would you use fit-content?
interview.answer: When you want a box to size to its content but never exceed a given maximum, like fit-content(300px).

interview.q: What does the box-decoration-break property control?
interview.answer: It decides whether borders, padding and backgrounds are applied per fragment or across the whole element when it breaks across lines or pages.

interview.q: Why might a box shadow be clipped by overflow: hidden?
interview.answer: The shadow paints outside the padding box, so an ancestor with overflow: hidden clips it unless you add padding or change overflow.

interview.q: What is the difference between margin and gap?
interview.answer: Margin pushes individual boxes apart and can collapse; gap adds space only between items in flex or grid containers and never collapses.

interview.q: How does gap behave in a single-column flex layout?
interview.answer: It adds vertical space between flex items without affecting the outer edges of the container.

interview.q: What is the effect of box-sizing on replaced elements like images?
interview.answer: It still applies, but the intrinsic size and aspect ratio of the replaced content may override the declared dimensions.

interview.q: Why should you avoid negative margins for layout in modern CSS?
interview.answer: They can pull elements out of flow and break stacking and spacing; flexbox and grid gap are clearer and safer.

interviewBank.q: display:none or visibility:hidden — which do you use?
interviewBank.answer: display:none removes the element from layout, accessibility and tab order. visibility:hidden keeps the space but hides the element. Choose by whether the space should exist.

interviewBank.q: What does inline-block give you that inline does not?
interviewBank.answer: It stays in the text flow like an inline box but accepts width, height and vertical margins, which makes it useful for chips and older nav patterns.

interviewBank.q: What is the default display of a div?
interviewBank.answer: block, so it takes the full available width and starts on a new line.

interviewBank.q: What is the default display of a span?
interviewBank.answer: inline, so it flows within text and only takes the space its content needs.

interviewBank.q: What does display: inline-block give you?
interviewBank.answer: An element that flows inline but accepts width, height and vertical padding like a block.

interviewBank.q: Why do inline-block elements leave a gap between them?
interviewBank.answer: Whitespace in the HTML source between the tags renders as a text space; remove the whitespace or set font-size: 0 on the parent.

interviewBank.q: What does display: none do to layout?
interviewBank.answer: It removes the element from the layout tree entirely, so siblings reflow as if it never existed.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between display: none and the hidden attribute?
interviewBank.answer: Both hide the element, but the hidden attribute is overridden by any display value in CSS, while display: none wins.

interviewBank.q: What does visibility: hidden preserve?
interviewBank.answer: The element's box and space in the layout, while making its rendering invisible.

interviewBank.q: When would you use visibility: hidden instead of display: none?
interviewBank.answer: When you need to reserve space, such as a placeholder that keeps a layout stable while content loads.

interviewBank.q: What does display: flex do to its children?
interviewBank.answer: It makes them flex items, laid out along a main axis with control over growth, shrink and alignment.

interviewBank.q: What does display: grid do to its children?
interviewBank.answer: It places them into rows and columns defined on the container, with explicit or implicit tracks.

interviewBank.q: What is display: contents?
interviewBank.answer: It removes the element's own box and promotes its children to participate in the parent's layout.

interviewBank.q: When is display: contents useful?
interviewBank.answer: For semantic wrappers that should not create an extra box, such as a list inside a flex container.

interviewBank.q: What accessibility risk does display: contents carry?
interviewBank.answer: In some browsers it can remove the element from the accessibility tree, so avoid it on interactive or semantic elements.

interviewBank.q: What does display: flow-root do?
interviewBank.answer: It creates a block formatting context without the side effects of overflow: hidden.

interviewBank.q: What is display: list-item?
interviewBank.answer: It makes an element generate a marker box, like a list item, in addition to its principal block box.

interviewBank.q: What does display: table do?
interviewBank.answer: It makes an element behave like a table element, enabling table layout without table markup.

interviewBank.q: What is display: run-in?
interviewBank.answer: A rarely supported value that merges a heading into the following paragraph; avoid relying on it.

interviewBank.q: What does display: inline-flex do?
interviewBank.answer: It creates an inline-level flex container, so it flows with text but lays out children with flexbox.

interviewBank.q: What does display: inline-grid do?
interviewBank.answer: It creates an inline-level grid container that flows with text while placing children in tracks.

interviewBank.q: How does display affect a floated element?
interviewBank.answer: A floated element computes to block (or similar) for layout purposes, so width and height apply even if it was inline.

interviewBank.q: How does display interact with position: absolute?
interviewBank.answer: Absolutely positioned elements compute to block-level boxes, so inline display becomes block.

interviewBank.q: What is the initial display value of most elements?
interviewBank.answer: inline for text-level elements and block for structural elements, according to the HTML user-agent stylesheet.

interviewBank.q: What is display: revert?
interviewBank.answer: It rolls the property back to the value from the previous origin, such as the user-agent or author stylesheet.

interviewBank.q: What is display: unset?
interviewBank.answer: It resets to the inherited value if the property inherits, otherwise to its initial value.

interviewBank.q: What is display: initial?
interviewBank.answer: It sets the property to its specification-defined initial value, which for display is inline.

interviewBank.q: What is display: inherit?
interviewBank.answer: It takes the computed display value from the parent element.

interviewBank.q: Why might a flex container's children ignore width?
interviewBank.answer: Flex items can grow or shrink by default, so an explicit width may be overridden by flex-basis and flex-grow.

interviewBank.q: What is flex-basis?
interviewBank.answer: The initial main-size of a flex item before free space is distributed by flex-grow and flex-shrink.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between justify-content and align-items?
interviewBank.answer: justify-content distributes space along the main axis; align-items aligns items along the cross axis.

interviewBank.q: What is align-content?
interviewBank.answer: It distributes space between wrapped lines in a multi-line flex or grid container.

interviewBank.q: What does flex-wrap: wrap do?
interviewBank.answer: It lets flex items move to the next line instead of shrinking to fit one line.

interviewBank.q: What is grid-template-columns?
interviewBank.answer: It defines the number and size of columns in an explicit grid.

interviewBank.q: What is grid-auto-flow?
interviewBank.answer: It controls how auto-placed items fill the grid, by row or by column.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between grid and inline-grid for accessibility?
interviewBank.answer: There is no accessibility difference; the choice only affects whether the container flows inline or block.

interviewBank.q: What does display: ruby do?
interviewBank.answer: It renders text with ruby annotations, used for East Asian pronunciation guides; rarely needed in Western layouts.

interviewBank.q: What does display: marker mean?
interviewBank.answer: It is an internal value used for list markers; authors do not set it directly.

interviewBank.q: Why might display: block on a button change its click area?
interviewBank.answer: A block button expands to the full width of its container, giving a larger tap target.

interviewBank.q: What is the effect of display on generated content?
interviewBank.answer: ::before and ::after create inline boxes by default, but their display can be changed to block or flex.

interviewBank.q: What does display: flex do to whitespace between items?
interviewBank.answer: It ignores source whitespace, so flex items sit flush without the inline-block gap.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between inline and inline-block for vertical alignment?
interviewBank.answer: inline elements align by the baseline of their text; inline-block boxes align by their last line box unless overridden.

interviewBank.q: What does vertical-align control?
interviewBank.answer: It aligns inline-level boxes and table cells relative to the line box or cell.

interviewBank.q: Why might an image leave a gap below it in a paragraph?
interviewBank.answer: Images are inline by default and sit on the text baseline, leaving space for descenders; set display: block or vertical-align: middle.

interviewBank.q: What is display: grid's effect on source order?
interviewBank.answer: Grid placement can visually reorder items without changing the DOM order, which can affect accessibility and tab order.

interviewBank.q: How do you hide an element but keep it readable by screen readers?
interviewBank.answer: Use a visually hidden pattern with clip and absolute positioning instead of display: none.

interviewBank.q: What does display: none do to an element's children?
interviewBank.answer: The entire subtree is removed from layout and rendering, including all descendants.

defenseBank.q: A learner tries to center a span with width.
defenseBank.answer: An inline box ignores width. Make it inline-block or put the centring on the block parent instead.

defenseBank.q: Why prefer flex over inline-block for navigation?
defenseBank.answer: Flex handles gaps, alignment and wrapping without whitespace artefacts between inline-blocks, and it keeps working when labels change length.

mcqBank.q: What is the default display of a div?
mcqBank.why: A div is a block-level element by default.

mcqBank.q: Which value removes an element from layout entirely?
mcqBank.why: Only display:none removes the box from layout.

interviewBank.q: Outline or border for focus?
interviewBank.answer: Outline, because it does not affect layout, can be offset from the edge, and is designed for focus indication. Removing it without a replacement breaks keyboard accessibility.

interviewBank.q: Why layer two box shadows?
interviewBank.answer: A tight, darker shadow suggests contact while a wide, lighter one suggests ambient light. Together they read as real depth without looking like a blurry halo.

interviewBank.q: What three values does a border shorthand need at minimum?
interviewBank.answer: Width, style and colour; omitting style makes the border invisible even if width and colour are set.

interviewBank.q: What is the default border-style?
interviewBank.answer: none, which is why no border appears until you set a style such as solid.

interviewBank.q: What does border: 0 do differently from border: none?
interviewBank.answer: Both remove the border, but border: 0 also resets the width to zero, which matters for form controls.

interviewBank.q: How do you round only the top corners of a box?
interviewBank.answer: Use border-radius with two values, or the longhand border-top-left-radius and border-top-right-radius.

interviewBank.q: What does a single value in border-radius do?
interviewBank.answer: It sets the radius of all four corners equally.

interviewBank.q: What does border-radius: 50% create?
interviewBank.answer: A circle when the box is square, or an ellipse when the box is rectangular.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between border and outline for focus styles?
interviewBank.answer: Border changes layout and box size; outline is drawn outside and does not affect layout, so it is safer for focus rings.

interviewBank.q: Why is outline-offset useful?
interviewBank.answer: It pushes the focus ring away from the element so it does not overlap content or get clipped.

interviewBank.q: What does box-shadow accept?
interviewBank.answer: Horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur radius, spread radius and colour, plus an optional inset keyword.

interviewBank.q: What does inset do in a box-shadow?
interviewBank.answer: It draws the shadow inside the box instead of outside, useful for pressed or recessed effects.

interviewBank.q: Why do multiple box-shadows not affect layout?
interviewBank.answer: Shadows are paint effects only; they do not create boxes or change dimensions.

interviewBank.q: How do you create a layered shadow?
interviewBank.answer: Comma-separate multiple shadow declarations, with the first on top.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between blur and spread?
interviewBank.answer: Blur softens the edge; spread grows or shrinks the shadow before blurring.

interviewBank.q: What does a negative spread do?
interviewBank.answer: It shrinks the shadow, which can create a sharp, smaller shadow behind the box.

interviewBank.q: Why might a box shadow be clipped?
interviewBank.answer: An ancestor with overflow: hidden clips it because the shadow paints outside the padding box.

interviewBank.q: What is text-shadow?
interviewBank.answer: A shadow applied to text glyphs, with offsets, blur and colour, similar to box-shadow but for text.

interviewBank.q: Can text-shadow be layered?
interviewBank.answer: Yes, comma-separate multiple shadows to create outlines or glow effects.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between border-color and outline-color?
interviewBank.answer: border-color colours the border box; outline-color colours the outline, which sits outside the border.

interviewBank.q: What does border-style: dashed do?
interviewBank.answer: It draws a dashed line; the dash pattern is browser-defined and cannot be customised in standard CSS.

interviewBank.q: What is border-image?
interviewBank.answer: It slices an image into nine parts and stretches or repeats them to form a border.

interviewBank.q: When is border-image useful?
interviewBank.answer: For decorative frames or ornaments that cannot be achieved with solid colours.

interviewBank.q: What does border-collapse do?
interviewBank.answer: It merges adjacent borders in a table into a single border.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between separate and collapse border models?
interviewBank.answer: Separate gives each cell its own border with spacing; collapse merges shared borders into one.

interviewBank.q: What does border-spacing control?
interviewBank.answer: The gap between cells in the separate border model.

interviewBank.q: Why might focus outlines be removed and what should replace them?
interviewBank.answer: Removing them hurts keyboard users; replace with a visible :focus-visible style instead of removing all focus styles.

interviewBank.q: What is :focus-visible?
interviewBank.answer: It matches when the browser decides a focus indicator should be shown, typically for keyboard navigation.

interviewBank.q: Why is :focus-visible better than :focus for mouse users?
interviewBank.answer: It avoids showing a focus ring on mouse clicks while keeping it for keyboard users.

interviewBank.q: What does clip-path do to an element's visible shape?
interviewBank.answer: It clips the element to a basic shape or polygon, hiding parts outside the path.

interviewBank.q: Does clip-path affect layout?
interviewBank.answer: No, the box keeps its original size; only the painted region is clipped.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between clip-path and mask?
interviewBank.answer: clip-path uses a vector path; mask uses an image with alpha or luminance to control visibility.

interviewBank.q: What does filter: drop-shadow do differently from box-shadow?
interviewBank.answer: It follows the alpha shape of the element, so it shadows transparent parts and non-rectangular shapes correctly.

interviewBank.q: Why use filter: drop-shadow on a PNG with transparency?
interviewBank.answer: Because box-shadow would draw a rectangle around the image, while drop-shadow follows the visible pixels.

interviewBank.q: What does border-radius do to a box-shadow?
interviewBank.answer: The shadow follows the rounded corners of the box.

interviewBank.q: What is a ridge or groove border?
interviewBank.answer: A 3D-effect border style that looks raised or carved; rarely used in modern designs.

interviewBank.q: What does outline-style: auto do?
interviewBank.answer: It lets the browser choose a platform-native outline style, often used for focus indicators.

interviewBank.q: Why might a border be invisible even with a width?
interviewBank.answer: If border-style is none or the colour matches the background, nothing is painted.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between border and box-shadow for a line?
interviewBank.answer: border is part of the box and affects size; box-shadow is paint-only and can create lines without layout changes.

interviewBank.q: How do you create a one-pixel divider without a border?
interviewBank.answer: Use a box-shadow with zero blur and a small spread, or a pseudo-element with a background.

interviewBank.q: What does border-top-style: hidden do?
interviewBank.answer: In the collapsing border model it suppresses the border; in the separate model it behaves like none.

interviewBank.q: Why is border-radius preferred over images for rounded corners?
interviewBank.answer: It scales, adapts to content and avoids extra HTTP requests.

interviewBank.q: What is the effect of a large border-radius on a small box?
interviewBank.answer: The corners overlap and the shape becomes a capsule or circle.

interviewBank.q: How do you create a capsule shape?
interviewBank.answer: Set border-radius to a value larger than half the height, such as 999px.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between border and outline for printing?
interviewBank.answer: Both print, but outlines may be omitted by some browsers; borders are reliable.

interviewBank.q: Why might box-shadow cause performance issues?
interviewBank.answer: Large blurs on many elements force expensive paint operations, especially during scroll or animation.

interviewBank.q: What does filter: blur do?
interviewBank.answer: It blurs the element and its children, often used for backgrounds or modal backdrops.

defenseBank.q: A designer asks for a 1px border that does not change size.
defenseBank.answer: A border adds to the box unless border-box is set. With border-box the border is drawn inside the declared width and the layout stays put.

defenseBank.q: Why not use box-shadow instead of a border?
defenseBank.answer: A shadow is paint only; it does not define the element’s edge, does not print reliably and cannot replace the visual boundary for high-contrast users.
steps: Show the shadow in forced colours.

mcqBank.q: Which border style must be present for a border to paint?
mcqBank.why: A visible style such as solid is required.

mcqBank.q: Which shadow draws inside the element?
mcqBank.why: The inset keyword draws the shadow inside the box.
