interview.answer: Removing them hurts keyboard users; replace with a visible :focus-visible style instead of removing all focus styles.

interview.q: What is :focus-visible?
interview.answer: It matches when the browser decides a focus indicator should be shown, typically for keyboard navigation.

interview.q: Why is :focus-visible better than :focus for mouse users?
interview.answer: It avoids showing a focus ring on mouse clicks while keeping it for keyboard users.

interview.q: What does clip-path do to an element's visible shape?
interview.answer: It clips the element to a basic shape or polygon, hiding parts outside the path.

interview.q: Does clip-path affect layout?
interview.answer: No, the box keeps its original size; only the painted region is clipped.

interview.q: What is the difference between clip-path and mask?
interview.answer: clip-path uses a vector path; mask uses an image with alpha or luminance to control visibility.

interview.q: What does filter: drop-shadow do differently from box-shadow?
interview.answer: It follows the alpha shape of the element, so it shadows transparent parts and non-rectangular shapes correctly.

interview.q: Why use filter: drop-shadow on a PNG with transparency?
interview.answer: Because box-shadow would draw a rectangle around the image, while drop-shadow follows the visible pixels.

interview.q: What does border-radius do to a box-shadow?
interview.answer: The shadow follows the rounded corners of the box.

interview.q: What is a ridge or groove border?
interview.answer: A 3D-effect border style that looks raised or carved; rarely used in modern designs.

interview.q: What does outline-style: auto do?
interview.answer: It lets the browser choose a platform-native outline style, often used for focus indicators.

interview.q: Why might a border be invisible even with a width?
interview.answer: If border-style is none or the colour matches the background, nothing is painted.

interview.q: What is the difference between border and box-shadow for a line?
interview.answer: border is part of the box and affects size; box-shadow is paint-only and can create lines without layout changes.

interview.q: How do you create a one-pixel divider without a border?
interview.answer: Use a box-shadow with zero blur and a small spread, or a pseudo-element with a background.

interview.q: What does border-top-style: hidden do?
interview.answer: In the collapsing border model it suppresses the border; in the separate model it behaves like none.

interview.q: Why is border-radius preferred over images for rounded corners?
interview.answer: It scales, adapts to content and avoids extra HTTP requests.

interview.q: What is the effect of a large border-radius on a small box?
interview.answer: The corners overlap and the shape becomes a capsule or circle.

interview.q: How do you create a capsule shape?
interview.answer: Set border-radius to a value larger than half the height, such as 999px.

interview.q: What is the difference between border and outline for printing?
interview.answer: Both print, but outlines may be omitted by some browsers; borders are reliable.

interview.q: Why might box-shadow cause performance issues?
interview.answer: Large blurs on many elements force expensive paint operations, especially during scroll or animation.

interview.q: What does filter: blur do?
interview.answer: It blurs the element and its children, often used for backgrounds or modal backdrops.

interviewBank.q: What containing block does an absolute element use?
interviewBank.answer: The nearest ancestor with a position other than static, or a transform, filter or container-type that establishes one. Without such an ancestor it uses the initial containing block.

interviewBank.q: How is sticky different from fixed?
interviewBank.answer: Sticky stays in normal flow until the scroll reaches its inset threshold, then behaves as if fixed within its containing block. Fixed is always relative to the viewport.

interviewBank.q: What does position: static do?
interviewBank.answer: It keeps the element in normal flow and ignores top, right, bottom and left.

interviewBank.q: What does position: relative do to layout?
interviewBank.answer: It keeps the element's space in normal flow but lets you offset it with top, right, bottom and left.

interviewBank.q: What space does an absolutely positioned element leave behind?
interviewBank.answer: None; it is removed from normal flow, so siblings reflow as if it were absent.

interviewBank.q: How do you find the containing block for an absolutely positioned element?
interviewBank.answer: Walk up the ancestors until you find one with a position other than static; if none exists, use the initial containing block.

interviewBank.q: What does position: fixed do?
interviewBank.answer: It positions the element relative to the viewport, so it stays in place while the page scrolls.

interviewBank.q: When does a fixed element not stay fixed to the viewport?
interviewBank.answer: When an ancestor has a transform, filter or perspective, which creates a new containing block for the fixed element.

interviewBank.q: What is position: sticky?
interviewBank.answer: A hybrid that behaves like relative until scroll crosses the given inset, then sticks within its containing block.

interviewBank.q: What limits how long a sticky element stays stuck?
interviewBank.answer: Its containing block; once that block scrolls past, the sticky element scrolls away with it.

interviewBank.q: What must you set for sticky to work?
interviewBank.answer: At least one of top, right, bottom or left, otherwise it behaves like relative.

interviewBank.q: How can you create a new stacking context deliberately?
interviewBank.answer: Use isolation: isolate, or position with z-index, transform, opacity below 1 or other triggering properties.

interviewBank.q: What does z-index do?
interviewBank.answer: It sets the stack level of a positioned or otherwise eligible element within its stacking context.

interviewBank.q: Why might a high z-index not bring an element forward?
interviewBank.answer: Because z-index is scoped to the nearest stacking context; a parent with a lower context traps it.

interviewBank.q: What creates a new stacking context?
interviewBank.answer: position with z-index, opacity below 1, transform, filter, clip-path, mask, isolation: isolate and several other properties.

interviewBank.q: What is isolation: isolate?
interviewBank.answer: It creates a new stacking context without changing layout, useful for containing z-index inside a component.

interviewBank.q: What is the default z-index?
interviewBank.answer: auto, which means the element does not create a new stacking context from z-index alone.

interviewBank.q: How do you stack elements without z-index?
interviewBank.answer: Later elements in source order paint on top of earlier ones within the same stacking context.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between top and margin-top?
interviewBank.answer: top offsets a positioned element without affecting flow; margin-top affects normal flow and can collapse.

interviewBank.q: What does inset: 0 do?
interviewBank.answer: It sets top, right, bottom and left to zero, stretching an absolutely positioned element to fill its containing block.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between absolute and fixed for modals?
interviewBank.answer: Absolute scrolls with the page unless the containing block is the viewport; fixed stays on screen, which suits overlays.

interviewBank.q: Why might a modal using position: fixed scroll with the page?
interviewBank.answer: Because an ancestor with transform creates a containing block, making fixed behave like absolute.

interviewBank.q: What is overflow: hidden's effect on positioning?
interviewBank.answer: It clips absolutely positioned descendants whose containing block is inside the overflow container.

interviewBank.q: What does position: relative do for z-index?
interviewBank.answer: It makes the element eligible for z-index and can create a stacking context when z-index is not auto.

interviewBank.q: What is the painting order of positioned elements?
interviewBank.answer: Positioned elements with z-index paint above non-positioned content; among them, stack level and source order decide.

interviewBank.q: What is a negative z-index used for?
interviewBank.answer: To place an element behind its parent's background, such as a decorative backdrop.

interviewBank.q: Why might a negative z-index element disappear?
interviewBank.answer: If the parent does not create a stacking context, the element paints behind the page background and becomes invisible.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between top: 50% and transform: translateY(-50%)?
interviewBank.answer: top moves the element by half the containing block height; transform then shifts it back by half its own height to centre it.

interviewBank.q: How do you centre an absolutely positioned element?
interviewBank.answer: Set top and left to 50%, then transform: translate(-50%, -50%) to offset by its own size.

interviewBank.q: What does position: absolute do to width?
interviewBank.answer: If left and right are both set, width is computed from them; otherwise it shrinks to fit content.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between left and inset-inline-start?
interviewBank.answer: left is physical; inset-inline-start is logical and adapts to writing direction.

interviewBank.q: Why prefer logical properties for positioned overlays?
interviewBank.answer: They adapt to right-to-left layouts without separate rules.

interviewBank.q: What does position: sticky do in a scroll container?
interviewBank.answer: It sticks relative to the nearest scroll ancestor, not necessarily the viewport.

interviewBank.q: What is the effect of height on a sticky element?
interviewBank.answer: A sticky element taller than its container cannot stick because there is no room to scroll within.

interviewBank.q: What is z-index: 0 used for?
interviewBank.answer: To create a stacking context without raising the element above siblings that have positive z-index.

interviewBank.q: What does position: relative preserve that absolute does not?
interviewBank.answer: Its original space in normal flow, so surrounding content does not reflow.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between fixed and absolute for a back-to-top button?
interviewBank.answer: Fixed stays on screen during scroll; absolute would scroll away unless the containing block is the viewport.

interviewBank.q: Why might position: fixed jitter during scroll?
interviewBank.answer: Because the browser repaints the fixed element on every scroll frame; transforms on ancestors can make it worse.

interviewBank.q: What is the containing block for a relatively positioned element?
interviewBank.answer: Itself; relative positioning offsets from its normal position, not from an ancestor.

interviewBank.q: What does top: 0 on a relative element do?
interviewBank.answer: It moves the element up by zero, leaving it in place but establishing it as positioned for z-index.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between z-index and order?
interviewBank.answer: z-index controls paint order; order controls flex and grid placement order, not paint stacking.

interviewBank.q: What does position: absolute do to margins?
interviewBank.answer: Margins still apply and can offset the element from its inset edges.

interviewBank.q: Why might an absolute element be clipped by a parent?
interviewBank.answer: If an ancestor has overflow: hidden and is the containing block or an ancestor of it, the element is clipped.

interviewBank.q: What is the initial containing block size?
interviewBank.answer: The viewport dimensions for continuous media, used when no positioned ancestor exists.

interviewBank.q: What does position: fixed do inside a transformed parent?
interviewBank.answer: It behaves like absolute relative to that parent, because the transform creates a containing block.

interviewBank.q: How do you prevent a fixed header from overlapping anchor targets?
interviewBank.answer: Use scroll-margin-top on the target or scroll-padding-top on the scroll container.

interviewBank.q: What is scroll-padding?
interviewBank.answer: It offsets scroll snap and anchor scrolling so fixed headers do not cover the target.

defenseBank.q: A learner uses absolute for the whole page layout.
defenseBank.answer: Absolute removes elements from flow, so nothing reserves their space and overlapping is inevitable. Flow, flex or grid should own layout; absolute is for overlays and badges.

defenseBank.q: Why does a huge z-index still sit behind?
defenseBank.answer: Stacking contexts compare siblings inside one context, not numbers across contexts. A parent with a lower context wins over every child inside it.
steps: Move the element to the right context.

interviewBank.q: Flexbox or Grid — how do you choose?
interviewBank.answer: Flexbox distributes items along one axis and is content-driven. Grid defines rows and columns together and is layout-driven. Use flex for a bar or a row of chips, grid for a page or gallery.

interviewBank.q: Why does a flex item refuse to shrink?
interviewBank.answer: A flex item’s automatic minimum size is its content size, so long unbreakable content can prevent shrinking. min-width:0 (or overflow handling) lets it shrink below that.

interviewBank.q: What is the main axis in flexbox?
interviewBank.answer: The primary direction along which flex items are laid out, controlled by flex-direction.

interviewBank.q: What is the cross axis?
interviewBank.answer: The axis perpendicular to the main axis, used for alignment with align-items and align-content.

interviewBank.q: What does flex-direction: row do?
interviewBank.answer: It lays items left to right in a horizontal main axis.

interviewBank.q: What does flex-direction: column do?
interviewBank.answer: It lays items top to bottom in a vertical main axis.

interviewBank.q: What is flex-wrap?
interviewBank.answer: It controls whether items wrap to a new line when they exceed the container width.

interviewBank.q: What does justify-content: space-between do?
interviewBank.answer: It places the first item at the start, the last at the end, and distributes equal space between the rest.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between space-around and space-evenly?
interviewBank.answer: space-around gives half-size gaps at the edges; space-evenly gives equal gaps everywhere including edges.

interviewBank.q: What does align-items: center do?
interviewBank.answer: It centres items along the cross axis within their line.

interviewBank.q: What is align-self?
interviewBank.answer: It overrides align-items for a single flex item.

interviewBank.q: What is flex-grow?
interviewBank.answer: It defines how much a flex item grows relative to others when free space is available.

interviewBank.q: What is flex-shrink?
interviewBank.answer: It defines how much a flex item shrinks relative to others when space is tight.

interviewBank.q: How does flex-basis differ from width in a flex item?
interviewBank.answer: flex-basis is the starting size before flex distribution and can be overridden by flex-grow; width is a fixed size.

interviewBank.q: What does flex: 1 do?
interviewBank.answer: It sets flex-grow: 1, flex-shrink: 1 and flex-basis: 0%, making items share space equally.

interviewBank.q: Why might flex: 1 cause overflow?
interviewBank.answer: Because flex-basis: 0 ignores content size, so long content can overflow unless min-width is handled.

interviewBank.q: What is min-width: 0 used for in flexbox?
interviewBank.answer: It lets a flex item shrink below its content size, preventing overflow in a row.

interviewBank.q: What is flex: auto?
interviewBank.answer: It sets flex-grow: 1, flex-shrink: 1 and flex-basis: auto, so items grow but start from their content size.

interviewBank.q: What is flex: none?
interviewBank.answer: It sets flex-grow: 0, flex-shrink: 0 and flex-basis: auto, making the item inflexible.

interviewBank.q: What does align-content do?
interviewBank.answer: It aligns wrapped lines along the cross axis in a multi-line flex container.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between align-items and align-content?
interviewBank.answer: align-items aligns items within a line; align-content aligns the lines themselves when wrapping.

interviewBank.q: What does order do?
interviewBank.answer: It changes the visual order of a flex item without changing the DOM order.

interviewBank.q: Why is order risky for accessibility?
interviewBank.answer: Screen readers and tab order follow the DOM, not the visual order, so mismatches confuse users.

interviewBank.q: What is gap in flexbox?
interviewBank.answer: It adds space between flex items without adding margins to the edges.

interviewBank.q: What does flex-direction: row-reverse do?
interviewBank.answer: It lays items right to left while keeping the main axis horizontal.

interviewBank.q: What does flex-direction: column-reverse do?
interviewBank.answer: It lays items bottom to top while keeping the main axis vertical.

interviewBank.q: What is the default flex-direction?
interviewBank.answer: row, so items flow horizontally by default.

interviewBank.q: What is the default flex-wrap?
interviewBank.answer: nowrap, so items stay on one line and shrink to fit.

interviewBank.q: What is the default justify-content?
interviewBank.answer: flex-start, so items pack toward the start of the main axis.

interviewBank.q: What is the default align-items?
interviewBank.answer: stretch, so items fill the cross axis of their line.

interviewBank.q: What is the default align-content?
interviewBank.answer: stretch, so wrapped lines fill the cross axis.

interviewBank.q: What does flex-basis: content do?
interviewBank.answer: It sizes the item based on its content, similar to max-content.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between width and flex-basis?
interviewBank.answer: width is a fixed size; flex-basis is the starting size before flex distribution and can be overridden by flex-grow.

interviewBank.q: What happens when flex items overflow?
interviewBank.answer: They overflow the container unless flex-wrap or flex-shrink allows them to fit.

interviewBank.q: How do you make a flex item not shrink?
interviewBank.answer: Set flex-shrink: 0, so it keeps its basis even when space is tight.

interviewBank.q: How do you make a flex item not grow?
interviewBank.answer: Set flex-grow: 0, so it does not absorb free space.

interviewBank.q: What is a flex container's main size?
interviewBank.answer: Its width in row direction or height in column direction, depending on flex-direction.

interviewBank.q: What is a flex item's cross size?
interviewBank.answer: Its height in row direction or width in column direction.

interviewBank.q: What does align-items: baseline do?
interviewBank.answer: It aligns items by their text baselines, useful for mixed font sizes.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between baseline and center alignment?
interviewBank.answer: baseline aligns text; center aligns the box midpoints, which can misalign text.

interviewBank.q: What does justify-content: center do?
interviewBank.answer: It centres items along the main axis with equal space on both sides.

interviewBank.q: What does justify-items do in flexbox?
interviewBank.answer: Nothing; justify-items is a grid property, not a flexbox property.

interviewBank.q: What is place-content?
interviewBank.answer: A shorthand for align-content and justify-content in grid and flexbox.

interviewBank.q: What is place-items?
interviewBank.answer: A shorthand for align-items and justify-items, mainly used in grid.

interviewBank.q: What is place-self?
interviewBank.answer: A shorthand for align-self and justify-self on a single grid item.

interviewBank.q: How do you vertically centre with flexbox?
interviewBank.answer: Set display: flex, align-items: center and justify-content: center on the container.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between a flex item and a flex container?
interviewBank.answer: A flex item is a child of a flex container; a flex container is the parent with display: flex.

defenseBank.q: A learner centres with margins.
defenseBank.answer: auto margins work in flex but are less explicit than justify-content and fail in wrapping or multi-line cases. Alignment properties express the intent.
steps: Add a second line and compare.

defenseBank.q: Why set gap instead of margins between items?
defenseBank.answer: Gap belongs to the container, so it does not add space at the outer edges and does not collapse. Margins have to be undone on the first or last child.

mcqBank.q: Which property aligns items on the cross axis?
mcqBank.why: align-items works across the cross axis.

mcqBank.q: What does flex: 1 mean?
mcqBank.why: It is the common shorthand for equal flexible items.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between auto-fit and auto-fill?
interviewBank.answer: auto-fill keeps empty tracks and leaves blank space; auto-fit collapses empty tracks so the existing items stretch to fill the row. Galleries usually want auto-fit.

interviewBank.q: What is the implicit grid?
interviewBank.answer: Tracks the browser creates automatically when items are placed outside the explicit template. It is why an extra item still lands somewhere sensible.

interviewBank.q: What is a grid container?
interviewBank.answer: An element with display: grid or inline-grid, which establishes a grid formatting context for its children.

interviewBank.q: What is a grid item?
interviewBank.answer: A direct child of a grid container, placed into the defined tracks.

interviewBank.q: How do you define responsive columns in grid?
interviewBank.answer: Use grid-template-columns with fr units and repeat with auto-fit or auto-fill.

interviewBank.q: What is grid-template-rows?
interviewBank.answer: It defines the number and size of rows in the explicit grid.

interviewBank.q: What is the fr unit?
interviewBank.answer: A flexible length that distributes free space in the grid proportionally among tracks.

interviewBank.q: What does grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr do?
interviewBank.answer: It creates three equal-width columns that share the available space.

interviewBank.q: What is gap in grid?
interviewBank.answer: It adds space between rows and columns without adding margins to the outer edges.

interviewBank.q: What is grid-column?
interviewBank.answer: A shorthand for grid-column-start and grid-column-end, placing an item across columns.

interviewBank.q: What is grid-row?
interviewBank.answer: A shorthand for grid-row-start and grid-row-end, placing an item across rows.

interviewBank.q: What does grid-area do?
interviewBank.answer: It places an item by naming a grid area or by specifying row and column lines.

interviewBank.q: What is a grid line?
interviewBank.answer: The dividing line between tracks, numbered from 1 and used for placement.

interviewBank.q: What is a grid track?
interviewBank.answer: A single row or column in the grid, sized by the template.

interviewBank.q: What is a grid cell?
interviewBank.answer: The intersection of a single row and column track.

interviewBank.q: What is a grid area?
interviewBank.answer: A rectangular region made of one or more cells, named in grid-template-areas.

interviewBank.q: What does auto-fit do?
interviewBank.answer: It creates as many tracks as fit in the container and collapses empty ones.

interviewBank.q: What does auto-fill do?
interviewBank.answer: It creates as many tracks as fit in the container but keeps empty ones.

interviewBank.q: When would you choose auto-fill over auto-fit in a responsive grid?
interviewBank.answer: Use auto-fill when you want to reserve track space for items that may be added later; use auto-fit when existing items should stretch to fill the row.

interviewBank.q: What does minmax() do?
interviewBank.answer: It sets a minimum and maximum size for a track, such as minmax(200px, 1fr).

interviewBank.q: What is repeat()?
interviewBank.answer: It repeats a track pattern, such as repeat(3, 1fr) for three equal columns.

interviewBank.q: What is auto-placement?
interviewBank.answer: The algorithm that places items without explicit coordinates, filling the grid in order.

interviewBank.q: How does grid-auto-flow affect item placement?
interviewBank.answer: It sets whether auto-placed items fill rows or columns first.

interviewBank.q: What is dense packing?
interviewBank.answer: grid-auto-flow: dense fills holes in the grid, which can reorder items visually.

interviewBank.q: What is an implicit grid?
interviewBank.answer: Tracks created automatically when items are placed outside the explicit grid.

interviewBank.q: What is grid-auto-rows?
interviewBank.answer: It sets the size of implicitly created rows.

interviewBank.q: What is grid-auto-columns?
interviewBank.answer: It sets the size of implicitly created columns.

interviewBank.q: What is subgrid?
interviewBank.answer: It lets a nested grid inherit its parent's track sizes for alignment across levels.

interviewBank.q: What is grid-template-areas?
interviewBank.answer: It names regions of the grid using ASCII-like rows of identifiers.

interviewBank.q: How do you create a named grid area?
interviewBank.answer: Define it in grid-template-areas and assign an item with grid-area: name.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between grid and flexbox?
interviewBank.answer: Grid is two-dimensional; flexbox is one-dimensional, though you can nest them.

interviewBank.q: When should you use grid over flexbox?
interviewBank.answer: When you need to control both rows and columns, such as page layouts and card grids.

interviewBank.q: What is justify-items?
interviewBank.answer: It aligns grid items along the inline axis within their cell.

interviewBank.q: What is align-items in grid?
interviewBank.answer: It aligns grid items along the block axis within their cell.

interviewBank.q: What is justify-content in grid?
interviewBank.answer: It aligns the whole grid along the inline axis when it is smaller than the container.

interviewBank.q: What is align-content in grid?
interviewBank.answer: It aligns the whole grid along the block axis when it is smaller than the container.

interviewBank.q: What is justify-self?
interviewBank.answer: It overrides justify-items for a single grid item.

interviewBank.q: What is align-self in grid?
interviewBank.answer: It overrides align-items for a single grid item.

interviewBank.q: What does span do in placement?
interviewBank.answer: It makes an item span multiple tracks, such as grid-column: span 2.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between 1 / 3 and span 2?
interviewBank.answer: 1 / 3 places from line 1 to line 3; span 2 starts at the auto position and spans two tracks.

interviewBank.q: What is the order property in grid?
interviewBank.answer: It changes the visual order of grid items without changing DOM order.

interviewBank.q: What is grid's effect on source order for accessibility?
interviewBank.answer: Visual reordering does not change tab or screen-reader order, so keep DOM order meaningful.

interviewBank.q: What is a min-content track?
interviewBank.answer: A track sized to the smallest size its content can take without overflow.

interviewBank.q: What is a max-content track?
interviewBank.answer: A track sized to the largest size its content needs without wrapping.

interviewBank.q: What is fit-content()?
interviewBank.answer: It clamps a track size between min-content and a given maximum.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between fixed and flexible tracks?
interviewBank.answer: Fixed tracks have a set size; flexible tracks using fr share free space.

interviewBank.q: How do you centre a grid item in its cell?
interviewBank.answer: Set justify-self: center and align-self: center, or use place-self: center.

defenseBank.q: A learner uses flex for a two-dimensional page.
defenseBank.answer: Flex aligns along one axis; a page with a header, sidebar and main area is two-dimensional. Grid expresses the rows and columns directly.
steps: Draw the layout as a grid.

defenseBank.q: Why use minmax in a gallery?
defenseBank.answer: It sets a floor so tiles never get too narrow and a ceiling of 1fr so they share the remaining space, which removes the need for breakpoints.

mcqBank.q: Which unit distributes free space in a grid?
mcqBank.why: The fr unit represents a fraction of the free space.

mcqBank.q: Which property names a grid area?
mcqBank.why: grid-area assigns an item to a named area or line span.

interview.q: What is the difference between auto-fit and auto-fill?
interview.answer: auto-fill keeps empty tracks and leaves blank space; auto-fit collapses empty tracks so the existing items stretch to fill the row. Galleries usually want auto-fit.

interview.q: What is the implicit grid?
interview.answer: Tracks the browser creates automatically when items are placed outside the explicit template. It is why an extra item still lands somewhere sensible.

interview.q: What is a grid container?
interview.answer: An element with display: grid or inline-grid, which establishes a grid formatting context for its children.

interview.q: What is a grid item?
interview.answer: A direct child of a grid container, placed into the defined tracks.

interview.q: How do you define responsive columns in grid?
interview.answer: Use grid-template-columns with fr units and repeat with auto-fit or auto-fill.

interview.q: What is grid-template-rows?
interview.answer: It defines the number and size of rows in the explicit grid.

interview.q: What is the fr unit?
interview.answer: A flexible length that distributes free space in the grid proportionally among tracks.

interview.q: What does grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr do?
interview.answer: It creates three equal-width columns that share the available space.

interview.q: What is gap in grid?
interview.answer: It adds space between rows and columns without adding margins to the outer edges.

interview.q: What is grid-column?
interview.answer: A shorthand for grid-column-start and grid-column-end, placing an item across columns.

interview.q: What is grid-row?
interview.answer: A shorthand for grid-row-start and grid-row-end, placing an item across rows.

interview.q: What does grid-area do?
interview.answer: It places an item by naming a grid area or by specifying row and column lines.

interview.q: What is a grid line?
interview.answer: The dividing line between tracks, numbered from 1 and used for placement.

interview.q: What is a grid track?
interview.answer: A single row or column in the grid, sized by the template.

interview.q: What is a grid cell?
interview.answer: The intersection of a single row and column track.

interview.q: What is a grid area?
interview.answer: A rectangular region made of one or more cells, named in grid-template-areas.

interview.q: What does auto-fit do?
interview.answer: It creates as many tracks as fit in the container and collapses empty ones.

interview.q: What does auto-fill do?
interview.answer: It creates as many tracks as fit in the container but keeps empty ones.

interview.q: When would you choose auto-fill over auto-fit in a responsive grid?
interview.answer: Use auto-fill when you want to reserve track space for items that may be added later; use auto-fit when existing items should stretch to fill the row.

interview.q: What does minmax() do?
interview.answer: It sets a minimum and maximum size for a track, such as minmax(200px, 1fr).

interview.q: What is repeat()?
interview.answer: It repeats a track pattern, such as repeat(3, 1fr) for three equal columns.

interview.q: What is auto-placement?
interview.answer: The algorithm that places items without explicit coordinates, filling the grid in order.

interview.q: How does grid-auto-flow affect item placement?
interview.answer: It sets whether auto-placed items fill rows or columns first.

interview.q: What is dense packing?
interview.answer: grid-auto-flow: dense fills holes in the grid, which can reorder items visually.

interview.q: What is an implicit grid?
interview.answer: Tracks created automatically when items are placed outside the explicit grid.

interview.q: What is grid-auto-rows?
interview.answer: It sets the size of implicitly created rows.

interview.q: What is grid-auto-columns?
interview.answer: It sets the size of implicitly created columns.

interview.q: What is subgrid?
interview.answer: It lets a nested grid inherit its parent's track sizes for alignment across levels.

interview.q: What is grid-template-areas?
interview.answer: It names regions of the grid using ASCII-like rows of identifiers.

interview.q: How do you create a named grid area?
interview.answer: Define it in grid-template-areas and assign an item with grid-area: name.

interview.q: What is the difference between grid and flexbox?
interview.answer: Grid is two-dimensional; flexbox is one-dimensional, though you can nest them.

interview.q: When should you use grid over flexbox?
interview.answer: When you need to control both rows and columns, such as page layouts and card grids.

interview.q: What is justify-items?
interview.answer: It aligns grid items along the inline axis within their cell.

interview.q: What is align-items in grid?
interview.answer: It aligns grid items along the block axis within their cell.

interview.q: What is justify-content in grid?
interview.answer: It aligns the whole grid along the inline axis when it is smaller than the container.

interview.q: What is align-content in grid?
interview.answer: It aligns the whole grid along the block axis when it is smaller than the container.

interview.q: What is justify-self?
interview.answer: It overrides justify-items for a single grid item.

interview.q: What is align-self in grid?
interview.answer: It overrides align-items for a single grid item.

interview.q: What does span do in placement?
interview.answer: It makes an item span multiple tracks, such as grid-column: span 2.

interview.q: What is the difference between 1 / 3 and span 2?
interview.answer: 1 / 3 places from line 1 to line 3; span 2 starts at the auto position and spans two tracks.

interview.q: What is the order property in grid?
interview.answer: It changes the visual order of grid items without changing DOM order.

interview.q: What is grid's effect on source order for accessibility?
interview.answer: Visual reordering does not change tab or screen-reader order, so keep DOM order meaningful.

interview.q: What is a min-content track?
interview.answer: A track sized to the smallest size its content can take without overflow.

interview.q: What is a max-content track?
interview.answer: A track sized to the largest size its content needs without wrapping.

interview.q: What is fit-content()?
interview.answer: It clamps a track size between min-content and a given maximum.

interview.q: What is the difference between fixed and flexible tracks?
interview.answer: Fixed tracks have a set size; flexible tracks using fr share free space.

interview.q: How do you centre a grid item in its cell?
interview.answer: Set justify-self: center and align-self: center, or use place-self: center.

interviewBank.q: Why mobile-first?
interviewBank.answer: The base styles target the smallest, most constrained layout, and min-width queries add capability. It keeps the default CSS simple and avoids undoing desktop rules on small screens.

interviewBank.q: When is a container query better than a media query?
interviewBank.answer: When a component’s layout depends on its own available width rather than the viewport — a card in a sidebar and the same card in a wide main column should adapt independently.

interviewBank.q: What is responsive web design?
interviewBank.answer: Designing layouts that adapt to different screen sizes, orientations and input methods using flexible grids, images and media queries.

interviewBank.q: What is a mobile-first approach?
interviewBank.answer: Writing base styles for small screens and adding complexity with min-width media queries for larger ones.

interviewBank.q: What is a desktop-first approach?
interviewBank.answer: Writing base styles for large screens and overriding with max-width media queries for smaller ones.

interviewBank.q: Why is mobile-first usually preferred?
interviewBank.answer: It starts with the smallest, most constrained layout and enhances progressively, which is easier to maintain.

interviewBank.q: What is a media query?
interviewBank.answer: A CSS rule that applies styles only when the device or viewport matches a condition such as width or orientation.

interviewBank.q: What is the viewport meta tag?
interviewBank.answer: It tells the browser to set the layout viewport width to the device width and initial scale to 1.

interviewBank.q: Why is the viewport meta tag necessary?
interviewBank.answer: Without it, mobile browsers assume a desktop-width viewport and zoom out, breaking responsive layouts.

interviewBank.q: What is a breakpoint?
interviewBank.answer: A viewport width at which the layout changes to better fit the available space.

interviewBank.q: Should breakpoints be based on devices or content?
interviewBank.answer: Content; choose widths where the layout breaks, not specific device sizes, so it stays future-proof.

interviewBank.q: What is a fluid layout?
interviewBank.answer: A layout that uses relative units and flexible containers so it adapts continuously instead of jumping at breakpoints.

interviewBank.q: What is clamp()?
interviewBank.answer: It constrains a value between a minimum and maximum, useful for fluid typography and spacing.

interviewBank.q: How do you make fluid type?
interviewBank.answer: Use font-size: clamp(1rem, 0.5rem + 1vw, 2rem) so text scales smoothly between bounds.

interviewBank.q: What is vw?
interviewBank.answer: A viewport-relative unit equal to 1% of the viewport width.

interviewBank.q: What is vh?
interviewBank.answer: A viewport-relative unit equal to 1% of the viewport height.

interviewBank.q: What is dvh?
interviewBank.answer: A dynamic viewport height unit that accounts for mobile browser chrome appearing and disappearing.

interviewBank.q: Why use dvh instead of vh on mobile?
interviewBank.answer: vh includes the area under the browser UI, causing layout jumps; dvh adjusts as the UI shows or hides.

interviewBank.q: What is an aspect-ratio media feature?
interviewBank.answer: It matches the ratio of width to height of the viewport.

interviewBank.q: What is orientation: landscape?
interviewBank.answer: A media feature that matches when the viewport is wider than it is tall.

interviewBank.q: What is prefers-color-scheme?
interviewBank.answer: A media feature that detects whether the user prefers a light or dark colour scheme.

interviewBank.q: What is prefers-reduced-motion?
interviewBank.answer: A media feature that detects whether the user wants reduced animation, used to disable motion.

interviewBank.q: How do you make images responsive?
interviewBank.answer: Set max-width: 100% and height: auto, and use srcset and sizes for different resolutions.

interviewBank.q: What is srcset?
interviewBank.answer: An HTML attribute listing image sources with widths so the browser picks the best one.

interviewBank.q: What is the sizes attribute?
interviewBank.answer: It tells the browser the display size of the image at each breakpoint so it can choose from srcset.

interviewBank.q: What is the picture element?
interviewBank.answer: It lets you provide multiple sources with media queries, such as art-directed images or modern formats.

interviewBank.q: What is a responsive container?
interviewBank.answer: A container with a max-width and auto margins, so it centres and stops growing on large screens.

interviewBank.q: What is min()?
interviewBank.answer: A function that returns the smaller of two values, useful for responsive sizing.

interviewBank.q: What is max()?
interviewBank.answer: A function that returns the larger of two values, useful for enforcing minimum sizes.

interviewBank.q: What is a fluid grid?
interviewBank.answer: A grid using fr units and auto-fit/minmax so columns reflow without media queries.

interviewBank.q: What is container query?
interviewBank.answer: A query that applies styles based on a container's size rather than the viewport.

interviewBank.q: Why are container queries useful?
interviewBank.answer: They let components respond to their own available space, making them reusable in different layouts.

interviewBank.q: What is @container?
interviewBank.answer: The at-rule that defines a container query.

interviewBank.q: What is container-type?
interviewBank.answer: It establishes a container for size queries, such as inline-size.

interviewBank.q: What is container-name?
interviewBank.answer: It names a container so queries can target it specifically.

interviewBank.q: What is a responsive table?
interviewBank.answer: A table that scrolls horizontally or reflows into cards on small screens to avoid overflow.

interviewBank.q: What is overflow-x: auto on a table wrapper?
interviewBank.answer: It lets a wide table scroll horizontally instead of breaking the page layout.

interviewBank.q: What is touch-action?
interviewBank.answer: It controls how touch gestures are handled, such as pan and pinch, to avoid conflicts with custom interactions.

interviewBank.q: What is -webkit-text-size-adjust?
interviewBank.answer: It prevents mobile browsers from automatically inflating text size in landscape mode.

interviewBank.q: What is a responsive navigation pattern?
interviewBank.answer: A nav that collapses into a menu on small screens, often with a toggle button.

interviewBank.q: What is a hamburger menu?
interviewBank.answer: A button with three lines that toggles a collapsed navigation on small screens.

interviewBank.q: What is the risk of hiding navigation behind a hamburger?
interviewBank.answer: Discoverability drops; ensure the toggle is accessible and the menu is keyboard-navigable.

interviewBank.q: What is srcset with x descriptors?
interviewBank.answer: It provides images for different device pixel ratios, such as 1x and 2x.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between w and x descriptors in srcset?
interviewBank.answer: w describes width in pixels; x describes device pixel ratio.

interviewBank.q: What is a responsive spacer?
interviewBank.answer: Spacing that scales with the viewport, such as margin using clamp or vw.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between em and vw for responsive spacing?
interviewBank.answer: em tracks font size; vw tracks viewport width, so they respond to different changes.

interviewBank.q: What is a breakpoint-less responsive design?
interviewBank.answer: A design that adapts fluidly using clamp, minmax and flex/grid without explicit media queries.

defenseBank.q: A learner picks breakpoints from device names.
defenseBank.answer: Devices change every year and the layout only cares about its own width. I resize until the content breaks, then put the query there.
steps: Add the query at that width.

defenseBank.q: Why set max-width 100% on images?
defenseBank.answer: An image with intrinsic width larger than its container overflows and causes horizontal scrolling. max-width plus height auto keeps it fluid and proportional.

mcqBank.q: Which query targets screens at least 640px wide?
mcqBank.why: min-width matches that width and above.

mcqBank.q: Which meta tag is required for mobile layout?
mcqBank.why: Without it mobile browsers use a virtual desktop width.

interviewBank.q: :focus or :focus-visible?
interviewBank.answer: :focus matches every focus, including a mouse click. :focus-visible matches when the browser judges that focus should be visible, which is usually keyboard navigation. Use it for rings.

interviewBank.q: Why does :where exist when :is can do the same grouping?
interviewBank.answer: :where always contributes zero specificity, which makes it ideal for resets and base styles that must not outrank component rules.

interviewBank.q: What is a pseudo-class?
interviewBank.answer: A keyword added to a selector that targets an element in a particular state or position, such as :hover or :first-child.

interviewBank.q: How does a pseudo-class differ from a pseudo-element in CSS?
interviewBank.answer: A pseudo-class filters existing elements by state; a pseudo-element generates or targets a sub-part of an element.

interviewBank.q: What does :hover do?
interviewBank.answer: It matches when the user's pointer is over the element.

interviewBank.q: What does :focus do?
interviewBank.answer: It matches when the element has keyboard or programmatic focus.

interviewBank.q: Why prefer :focus-visible over :focus for form controls?
interviewBank.answer: It shows a focus ring for keyboard users while avoiding it on mouse clicks.

interviewBank.q: What is :focus-within?
interviewBank.answer: It matches an element that contains a focused descendant.

interviewBank.q: What does :active do?
interviewBank.answer: It matches while the element is being activated, such as during a mouse press.

interviewBank.q: What does :visited do?
interviewBank.answer: It matches links the user has already visited, with strict styling limits for privacy.

interviewBank.q: Why are :visited styles restricted?
interviewBank.answer: To prevent scripts from reading visited links through computed styles, which would leak browsing history.

interviewBank.q: What does :checked match?
interviewBank.answer: Checked checkboxes, radio buttons and selected option elements.

interviewBank.q: What does :disabled match?
interviewBank.answer: Form controls that are disabled and cannot be interacted with.

interviewBank.q: What does :enabled match?
interviewBank.answer: Form controls that are not disabled.

interviewBank.q: What does :required match?
interviewBank.answer: Form controls with the required attribute.

interviewBank.q: What does :optional match?
interviewBank.answer: Form controls without the required attribute.

interviewBank.q: What does :valid match?
interviewBank.answer: Form controls whose value satisfies their validation constraints.

interviewBank.q: What does :invalid match?
interviewBank.answer: Form controls whose value fails validation.

interviewBank.q: What does :in-range match?
interviewBank.answer: Inputs whose value is within the min and max range.

interviewBank.q: What does :out-of-range match?
interviewBank.answer: Inputs whose value is outside the min and max range.

interviewBank.q: What does :placeholder-shown match?
interviewBank.answer: Inputs currently showing their placeholder text.

interviewBank.q: What does :first-child match?
interviewBank.answer: An element that is the first child of its parent.

interviewBank.q: What does :last-child match?
interviewBank.answer: An element that is the last child of its parent.

interviewBank.q: What does :nth-child() do?
interviewBank.answer: It matches children by position using a formula such as 2n+1 for odd children.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between :nth-child and :nth-of-type?
interviewBank.answer: :nth-child counts all siblings; :nth-of-type counts only siblings of the same element type.

interviewBank.q: When is :only-child useful in component styling?
interviewBank.answer: It styles an element differently when it has no siblings, such as a lone list item.

interviewBank.q: What does :empty match?
interviewBank.answer: An element with no children, including no text nodes.

interviewBank.q: How does :not() differ from :is() and :where()?
interviewBank.answer: :not() excludes matching elements, while :is() and :where() include them.

interviewBank.q: What does :is() do?
interviewBank.answer: It matches any element matching one of the listed selectors, with the specificity of the most specific argument.

interviewBank.q: What does :where() do?
interviewBank.answer: Like :is() but with zero specificity, useful for low-specificity defaults.

interviewBank.q: What does :has() do?
interviewBank.answer: It matches an element that has a descendant or sibling matching the given selector, enabling parent selection.

interviewBank.q: Why is :has() called the parent selector?
interviewBank.answer: Because it lets you style a parent based on its children, which was previously impossible in CSS.

interviewBank.q: What is :nth-last-child()?
interviewBank.answer: It counts children from the end instead of the beginning.

interviewBank.q: What is :nth-last-of-type()?
interviewBank.answer: It counts siblings of the same type from the end.

interviewBank.q: What does :first-of-type match?
interviewBank.answer: The first sibling of its element type within its parent.

interviewBank.q: What does :last-of-type match?
interviewBank.answer: The last sibling of its element type within its parent.

interviewBank.q: What does :only-of-type match?
interviewBank.answer: An element that is the only sibling of its type within its parent.

interviewBank.q: What is :root?
interviewBank.answer: It matches the document root element, usually html, and is often used for CSS variables.

interviewBank.q: What is :target?
interviewBank.answer: It matches the element whose id matches the URL fragment.

interviewBank.q: What does :lang() do?
interviewBank.answer: It matches elements based on their language attribute or inherited language.

interviewBank.q: What is :dir()?
interviewBank.answer: It matches elements based on text direction, such as ltr or rtl.

interviewBank.q: What does :default match?
interviewBank.answer: The default option in a select or the default submit button in a form.

interviewBank.q: What does :indeterminate match?
interviewBank.answer: Checkboxes or radio buttons in an indeterminate state, or progress elements.

interviewBank.q: What does :read-only match?
interviewBank.answer: Form controls that cannot be edited, such as those with readonly.

interviewBank.q: What does :read-write match?
interviewBank.answer: Form controls that can be edited.

interviewBank.q: What is the specificity of :is()?
interviewBank.answer: The specificity of its most specific argument, which can make it unexpectedly strong.

interviewBank.q: What is the specificity of :where()?
interviewBank.answer: Zero, so it never increases specificity.

defenseBank.q: A designer wants the focus ring removed.
defenseBank.answer: The ring is the only signal a keyboard user has. We can restyle it to match the brand, but not remove it.

defenseBank.q: When is :has the right tool?
defenseBank.answer: When a parent must react to a child’s state and no class is being set by script, such as marking a field wrapper invalid. Where script already sets a class, that class is simpler.

mcqBank.q: Which pseudo-class matches every second list item?
mcqBank.why: 2n matches positions 2, 4, 6 and so on.

mcqBank.q: Which selector adds no specificity?
mcqBank.why: :where() always has zero specificity.

interviewBank.q: Why does ::before need a content property?
interviewBank.answer: Generated boxes only exist when content is set, even an empty string. Without it the pseudo-element has no box to style.

interviewBank.q: Is generated content accessible?
interviewBank.answer: It is read by some screen readers depending on the content and browser, and it is not reliably selectable or translatable. Real content belongs in the markup.

interviewBank.q: What is a pseudo-element?
interviewBank.answer: A keyword that lets you style a specific part of an element or insert generated content, such as ::before or ::first-line.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between ::before and ::after?
interviewBank.answer: ::before inserts content before the element's own content; ::after inserts it after.

interviewBank.q: What must ::before and ::after have to render?
interviewBank.answer: A content property; without it the pseudo-element is not generated.

interviewBank.q: Are ::before and ::after inline by default?
interviewBank.answer: Yes, they generate inline boxes unless you change their display.

interviewBank.q: What is ::first-line?
interviewBank.answer: It targets the first formatted line of a block, with only a subset of properties allowed.

interviewBank.q: What is ::first-letter?
interviewBank.answer: It targets the first letter or character of a block, often used for drop caps.

interviewBank.q: What is ::selection?
interviewBank.answer: It styles the portion of text highlighted by the user.

interviewBank.q: What is ::placeholder?
interviewBank.answer: It styles the placeholder text of an input or textarea.

interviewBank.q: What is ::marker?
interviewBank.answer: It styles the marker box of a list item, such as the bullet or number.

interviewBank.q: What is ::backdrop?
interviewBank.answer: It styles the backdrop behind a dialog or popover in the top layer.

interviewBank.q: What is ::file-selector-button?
interviewBank.answer: It styles the button inside an input type=file control.

interviewBank.q: What is ::cue?
interviewBank.answer: It styles WebVTT captions in video or audio elements.

interviewBank.q: What is ::slotted()?
interviewBank.answer: It styles elements distributed into a slot in a shadow DOM.

interviewBank.q: What is ::part()?
interviewBank.answer: It styles a part exposed by a shadow DOM component via the part attribute.

interviewBank.q: What are the single-colon pseudo-elements?
interviewBank.answer: Legacy forms like :before and :first-line that browsers still support for backwards compatibility.

interviewBank.q: Why use double colons for pseudo-elements?
interviewBank.answer: To distinguish them from pseudo-classes, as the specification recommends.

interviewBank.q: Can ::before create an image?
interviewBank.answer: Yes, with content: url(...), though it is better to use a real img for meaningful images.

interviewBank.q: What is generated content used for?
interviewBank.answer: Decorative icons, clearfix hacks, counters and quote marks without extra markup.

interviewBank.q: What are CSS counters?
interviewBank.answer: Automatic numbering managed with counter-reset, counter-increment and content: counter().

interviewBank.q: How do you create a numbered list with counters?
interviewBank.answer: Reset a counter on the parent, increment it on each item and display it with ::before and content.

interviewBank.q: What is counter-reset?
interviewBank.answer: It creates or resets a named counter to a starting value, usually 0.

interviewBank.q: What is counter-increment?
interviewBank.answer: It increases a named counter by a given amount, defaulting to 1.

interviewBank.q: Can counters be nested?
interviewBank.answer: Yes, by resetting a counter inside a child, creating independent numbering per section.

interviewBank.q: What is content: attr()?
interviewBank.answer: It inserts the value of an HTML attribute into generated content.

interviewBank.q: What is content: open-quote?
interviewBank.answer: It inserts the opening quotation mark for the current language.

interviewBank.q: What is content: close-quote?
interviewBank.answer: It inserts the closing quotation mark for the current language.

interviewBank.q: What is content: no-open-quote?
interviewBank.answer: It increments the quote level without inserting a mark, useful for nested quotes.

interviewBank.q: What is content: ''?
interviewBank.answer: It generates an empty pseudo-element, useful for decorative boxes or clearfix.

interviewBank.q: What is the clearfix hack?
interviewBank.answer: Using ::after with content: '' and display: block to clear floats after a container.

interviewBank.q: Why is clearfix less needed now?
interviewBank.answer: Flexbox and grid do not collapse floats the way block flow does.

interviewBank.q: What properties can ::first-line style?
interviewBank.answer: Font, colour, background, word-spacing, letter-spacing, text-decoration, text-transform, line-height and text-shadow.

interviewBank.q: What properties can ::first-letter style?
interviewBank.answer: Float, font, colour, background, margin, padding, border, text-decoration and text-transform.

interviewBank.q: Why is ::selection limited?
interviewBank.answer: Only colour and background are widely supported; other properties are ignored for security and consistency.

interviewBank.q: What is ::placeholder colour default?
interviewBank.answer: A light grey, but it can be overridden with ::placeholder.

interviewBank.q: What is the opacity of ::placeholder usually?
interviewBank.answer: Often around 0.5 to 0.7 depending on the browser, so explicit styling is safer.

interviewBank.q: What does ::marker support?
interviewBank.answer: Colour, font, content and a few text properties; layout properties are not allowed.

interviewBank.q: Can ::marker be replaced with an image?
interviewBank.answer: Not directly; use list-style-image on the list or a ::before pseudo-element for full control.

interviewBank.q: What is ::backdrop used for?
interviewBank.answer: Styling the dimmed background behind a modal dialog or fullscreen element.

interviewBank.q: What is the top layer?
interviewBank.answer: A special rendering layer above all other content, used by dialogs, popovers and full-screen elements.

interviewBank.q: What is ::details-content?
interviewBank.answer: It targets the content box of a details element when open, in supporting browsers.

interviewBank.q: What is ::spelling-error?
interviewBank.answer: It styles text flagged by the browser's spell checker, in supporting browsers.

interviewBank.q: What is ::grammar-error?
interviewBank.answer: It styles text flagged by the browser's grammar checker, in supporting browsers.

interviewBank.q: What is ::target-text?
interviewBank.answer: It styles text highlighted by text fragments in the URL.

interviewBank.q: What is ::view-transition?
interviewBank.answer: It styles the root of a view transition, used for page or element transitions.

interviewBank.q: What is ::view-transition-old and ::view-transition-new?
interviewBank.answer: They style the outgoing and incoming snapshots during a view transition.

defenseBank.q: A learner puts the entire button label in ::before.
defenseBank.answer: If the generated content fails, the control has no label, and it may not be exposed correctly. The label belongs in the markup; pseudo-elements are decoration.
steps: Move the label into the element.

defenseBank.q: Why prefer a real element over an overlay pseudo-element?
defenseBank.answer: A pseudo-element cannot receive events or be individually selected or announced, so anything interactive needs a real element.

mcqBank.q: Which pseudo-element styles the first line of a paragraph?
mcqBank.why: ::first-line targets the first formatted line.

mcqBank.q: Which property is required for ::after to render?

interview.q: Why does ::before need a content property?
interview.answer: Generated boxes only exist when content is set, even an empty string. Without it the pseudo-element has no box to style.

interview.q: Is generated content accessible?
interview.answer: It is read by some screen readers depending on the content and browser, and it is not reliably selectable or translatable. Real content belongs in the markup.

interview.q: What is a pseudo-element?
interview.answer: A keyword that lets you style a specific part of an element or insert generated content, such as ::before or ::first-line.

interview.q: What is the difference between ::before and ::after?
interview.answer: ::before inserts content before the element's own content; ::after inserts it after.

interview.q: What must ::before and ::after have to render?
interview.answer: A content property; without it the pseudo-element is not generated.

interview.q: Are ::before and ::after inline by default?
interview.answer: Yes, they generate inline boxes unless you change their display.

interview.q: What is ::first-line?
interview.answer: It targets the first formatted line of a block, with only a subset of properties allowed.

interview.q: What is ::first-letter?
interview.answer: It targets the first letter or character of a block, often used for drop caps.

interview.q: What is ::selection?
interview.answer: It styles the portion of text highlighted by the user.

interview.q: What is ::placeholder?
interview.answer: It styles the placeholder text of an input or textarea.

interview.q: What is ::marker?
interview.answer: It styles the marker box of a list item, such as the bullet or number.

interview.q: What is ::backdrop?
interview.answer: It styles the backdrop behind a dialog or popover in the top layer.

interview.q: What is ::file-selector-button?
interview.answer: It styles the button inside an input type=file control.

interview.q: What is ::cue?
interview.answer: It styles WebVTT captions in video or audio elements.

interview.q: What is ::slotted()?
interview.answer: It styles elements distributed into a slot in a shadow DOM.

interview.q: What is ::part()?
interview.answer: It styles a part exposed by a shadow DOM component via the part attribute.

interview.q: What are the single-colon pseudo-elements?
interview.answer: Legacy forms like :before and :first-line that browsers still support for backwards compatibility.

interview.q: Why use double colons for pseudo-elements?
interview.answer: To distinguish them from pseudo-classes, as the specification recommends.

interview.q: Can ::before create an image?
interview.answer: Yes, with content: url(...), though it is better to use a real img for meaningful images.

interview.q: What is generated content used for?
interview.answer: Decorative icons, clearfix hacks, counters and quote marks without extra markup.

interview.q: What are CSS counters?
interview.answer: Automatic numbering managed with counter-reset, counter-increment and content: counter().

interview.q: How do you create a numbered list with counters?
interview.answer: Reset a counter on the parent, increment it on each item and display it with ::before and content.

interview.q: What is counter-reset?
interview.answer: It creates or resets a named counter to a starting value, usually 0.

interview.q: What is counter-increment?
interview.answer: It increases a named counter by a given amount, defaulting to 1.

interview.q: Can counters be nested?
interview.answer: Yes, by resetting a counter inside a child, creating independent numbering per section.

interview.q: What is content: attr()?
interview.answer: It inserts the value of an HTML attribute into generated content.

interview.q: What is content: open-quote?
interview.answer: It inserts the opening quotation mark for the current language.

interview.q: What is content: close-quote?
interview.answer: It inserts the closing quotation mark for the current language.

interview.q: What is content: no-open-quote?
interview.answer: It increments the quote level without inserting a mark, useful for nested quotes.

interview.q: What is content: ''?
interview.answer: It generates an empty pseudo-element, useful for decorative boxes or clearfix.

interview.q: What is the clearfix hack?
interview.answer: Using ::after with content: '' and display: block to clear floats after a container.

interview.q: Why is clearfix less needed now?
interview.answer: Flexbox and grid do not collapse floats the way block flow does.

interview.q: What properties can ::first-line style?
interview.answer: Font, colour, background, word-spacing, letter-spacing, text-decoration, text-transform, line-height and text-shadow.

interview.q: What properties can ::first-letter style?
interview.answer: Float, font, colour, background, margin, padding, border, text-decoration and text-transform.

interview.q: Why is ::selection limited?
interview.answer: Only colour and background are widely supported; other properties are ignored for security and consistency.

interview.q: What is ::placeholder colour default?
interview.answer: A light grey, but it can be overridden with ::placeholder.

interview.q: What is the opacity of ::placeholder usually?
interview.answer: Often around 0.5 to 0.7 depending on the browser, so explicit styling is safer.

interview.q: What does ::marker support?
interview.answer: Colour, font, content and a few text properties; layout properties are not allowed.

interview.q: Can ::marker be replaced with an image?
interview.answer: Not directly; use list-style-image on the list or a ::before pseudo-element for full control.

interview.q: What is ::backdrop used for?
interview.answer: Styling the dimmed background behind a modal dialog or fullscreen element.

interview.q: What is the top layer?
interview.answer: A special rendering layer above all other content, used by dialogs, popovers and full-screen elements.

interview.q: What is ::details-content?
interview.answer: It targets the content box of a details element when open, in supporting browsers.

interview.q: What is ::spelling-error?
interview.answer: It styles text flagged by the browser's spell checker, in supporting browsers.

interview.q: What is ::grammar-error?
interview.answer: It styles text flagged by the browser's grammar checker, in supporting browsers.

interview.q: What is ::target-text?
interview.answer: It styles text highlighted by text fragments in the URL.

interview.q: What is ::view-transition?
interview.answer: It styles the root of a view transition, used for page or element transitions.

interview.q: What is ::view-transition-old and ::view-transition-new?
interview.answer: They style the outgoing and incoming snapshots during a view transition.

topics.title: Transitions need four decisions
topics.body: Transition property, duration, timing function aur delay batata hai. Sirf un properties par lagta hai jinke beech browser interpolate kar sakta hai.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Transition</title>
  <style>
    .btn { background: #2563eb; color: #fff; padding: 10px 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; transition: background-color 180ms ease, transform 180ms ease; }
    .btn:hover { background: #1d4ed8; transform: translateY(-2px); }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="btn" type="button">Hover me</button>
</body>
</html>

interviewBank.q: Which properties are cheap to animate?
interviewBank.answer: transform and opacity, because they can be handled on the compositor without layout or paint. Animating width, top or box-shadow forces more work each frame.

interviewBank.q: What does transform do to layout?
interviewBank.answer: Nothing. It changes the visual rendering after layout, so neighbours do not move and the original space is preserved.

interviewBank.q: What is a CSS transition?
interviewBank.answer: A smooth change between two states of a property over a given duration.

interviewBank.q: What properties can transition?
interviewBank.answer: Those that can be interpolated, such as colour, length, transform and opacity; display cannot in standard CSS.

interviewBank.q: What is the transition-property?
interviewBank.answer: It names which CSS properties should animate when they change.

interviewBank.q: What does transition-duration control?
interviewBank.answer: How long the transition takes to complete.

interviewBank.q: What is transition-timing-function?
interviewBank.answer: It defines the acceleration curve, such as ease, linear or a cubic-bezier.

interviewBank.q: What is transition-delay?
interviewBank.answer: It waits a specified time before starting the transition.

interviewBank.q: What is the transition shorthand?
interviewBank.answer: property duration timing-function delay, in that order.

interviewBank.q: Why is transition: all considered risky?
interviewBank.answer: It animates every changing property, which can cause unexpected and janky animations.

interviewBank.q: What is transform?
interviewBank.answer: A property that moves, rotates, scales or skews an element without affecting layout.

interviewBank.q: What does transform: translate() do?
interviewBank.answer: It moves an element by a given horizontal and vertical offset.

interviewBank.q: What does transform: rotate() do?
interviewBank.answer: It rotates an element around its transform origin by a given angle.

interviewBank.q: What does transform: scale() do?
interviewBank.answer: It enlarges or shrinks an element uniformly or per axis.

interviewBank.q: What does transform: skew() do?
interviewBank.answer: It slants an element along the x or y axis.

interviewBank.q: Why does transform not cause reflow?
interviewBank.answer: It is a paint and composite effect applied after layout, so siblings do not move.

interviewBank.q: What is transform-origin?
interviewBank.answer: The point around which transforms such as rotate and scale are applied.

interviewBank.q: What is the default transform-origin?
interviewBank.answer: 50% 50%, the centre of the element.

interviewBank.q: What does transform-style: preserve-3d do?
interviewBank.answer: It lets child elements participate in the parent's 3D space.

interviewBank.q: What is perspective?
interviewBank.answer: It sets the distance between the viewer and the z=0 plane, creating a 3D effect.

interviewBank.q: What is perspective-origin?
interviewBank.answer: The point from which the viewer looks at the 3D scene.

interviewBank.q: What is backface-visibility?
interviewBank.answer: It controls whether the back of a rotated element is visible.

interviewBank.q: What does translate3d do?
interviewBank.answer: It moves an element in 3D space and often promotes it to its own compositing layer.

interviewBank.q: Why use transform instead of top and left for animation?
interviewBank.answer: Transforms are compositor-friendly and avoid layout and paint, so they are smoother.

interviewBank.q: What is will-change?
interviewBank.answer: A hint to the browser that an element will change, allowing it to prepare resources in advance.

interviewBank.q: Why is will-change overuse harmful?
interviewBank.answer: It consumes memory and can degrade performance if applied to too many elements.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between transition and animation?
interviewBank.answer: Transitions run between two states triggered by a change; animations run keyframes on a timeline.

interviewBank.q: What does transitionend event do?
interviewBank.answer: It fires when a transition finishes, letting JavaScript react to the completed animation.

interviewBank.q: What happens if a property changes mid-transition?
interviewBank.answer: The browser starts a new transition from the current intermediate value.

interviewBank.q: What is a cubic-bezier curve?
interviewBank.answer: A timing function defined by four control points, allowing custom acceleration.

interviewBank.q: What is ease-in-out?
interviewBank.answer: A timing function that starts and ends slowly, speeding up in the middle.

interviewBank.q: What is steps()?
interviewBank.answer: A timing function that jumps between discrete steps instead of interpolating smoothly.

interviewBank.q: When use steps()?
interviewBank.answer: For sprite animations or typewriter effects where discrete frames are desired.

interviewBank.q: What is transform: matrix()?
interviewBank.answer: A compact way to combine translate, scale, skew and rotate into one transform.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between translate and position?
interviewBank.answer: translate moves visually without layout changes; position changes layout and flow.

interviewBank.q: What is rotateX?
interviewBank.answer: It rotates an element around the horizontal axis, creating a 3D flip effect.

interviewBank.q: What is rotateY?
interviewBank.answer: It rotates an element around the vertical axis, creating a 3D turn effect.

interviewBank.q: What is scale3d?
interviewBank.answer: It scales an element in three dimensions independently.

interviewBank.q: What is skewX?
interviewBank.answer: It slants an element horizontally, distorting its shape.

interviewBank.q: What is skewY?
interviewBank.answer: It slants an element vertically, distorting its shape.

interviewBank.q: What is transform-box?
interviewBank.answer: It defines the reference box for percentage transforms and transform-origin.

interviewBank.q: What does transform-box: fill-box do?
interviewBank.answer: It uses the object's bounding box as the reference, common for SVG.

interviewBank.q: What is the composite property?
interviewBank.answer: It controls how animations compose with other transforms, such as replace or add.

interviewBank.q: What is animation-composition?
interviewBank.answer: It defines how multiple animations combine their transform values.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between translate and translate3d for performance?
interviewBank.answer: translate3d often forces GPU compositing; modern browsers treat translate similarly.

interviewBank.q: What is motion-path?
interviewBank.answer: It animates an element along a defined SVG path.

interviewBank.q: What is offset-path?
interviewBank.answer: The property that defines the path for motion-path animation.

defenseBank.q: A learner animates width for a progress bar.
defenseBank.answer: Animating width triggers layout on every frame. A transform scaleX on an inner bar gives the same visual with far less work.
steps: Show the layout cost in DevTools.

defenseBank.q: Why respect reduced motion?
defenseBank.answer: Large movement and parallax can cause nausea and vestibular symptoms. A prefers-reduced-motion query should remove or shorten non-essential motion.

mcqBank.q: Which property defines how long a transition takes?
mcqBank.why: Duration is the time the transition runs.

mcqBank.q: Which transform moves an element?
mcqBank.why: translate shifts position without affecting layout.

debug.title: A transition on display none
debug.code:
<style>
  .panel { display: none; transition: opacity 200ms ease; }
  .panel.open { display: block; opacity: 1; }
</style>
debug.error: display is not interpolable: the element jumps from no box to a box, so there are no intermediate frames to transition.
debug.fix:
<style>
  .panel { opacity: 0; visibility: hidden; transition: opacity 200ms ease, visibility 200ms; }
  .panel.open { opacity: 1; visibility: visible; }
</style>
debug.expected: Panel fades in over 200ms.
